journeys.sum: Austronesian-speaking farmers and voyagers spread from Taiwan through the Philippines towards the Moluccas, ancestors of the Lapita people.
First long open-sea crossing in human history, from the Philippines some 2,300 km to Guam and Saipan.

Starting world c. 1400 BC: the Aegean coasts and islands, Crete, Rhodes and western Anatolia, with contacts to Cyprus, the Levant coast, the Nile delta and Amarna, and Mycenaean trade points in southern Italy, the Aeolian islands and eastern Sicily.

journeys.n: Lapita culture in the Bismarck Archipelago
journeys.sum: The Lapita cultural complex, with its dentate-stamped pottery, appears in the Bismarck Archipelago (Mussau, New Britain, New Ireland).
Lapita voyagers settled the Loyalty Islands and Grande Terre, naming the type site at Lapita (Kone).
The Yellow River heartland of the Shang and Western Zhou: the Wei valley, the central plain, Shandong and Yan.

journeys.n: Lapita crossing into Remote Oceania (Reef and Santa Cruz)
journeys.sum: Lapita voyagers passed the inhabited main Solomons to settle the Reef and Santa Cruz Islands, the first step into Remote Oceania.
First settlement of Vanuatu, including the Teouma cemetery on Efate.
Settlement of Fiji from Vanuatu, the gateway to Polynesia; earliest site at Bourewa on Viti Levu.
First settlement of Tonga at Nukuleka on Tongatapu, the earliest site in Polynesia.

journeys.n: Lapita settlement of Wallis, Futuna and Samoa
journeys.sum: Lapita settlers reached Futuna, Uvea and Samoa (Mulifanua), completing the settlement of West Polynesia.
Phoenician settlement at Kition on Cyprus, the first step of Tyre's westward expansion.
Tyrians found Carthage on the Gulf of Tunis, opening the central Mediterranean sea route west.
Tyrian foundation of Gadir (Cadiz) beyond the Pillars of Heracles, the Phoenician gateway to the Atlantic and the silver of Tartessos.
Phoenician settlements at Caralis, Nora, Sulcis and Tharros along the southern and western coasts of Sardinia.
Phoenician colony of Utica on the Tunisian coast.

journeys.n: Euboean colonists of Chalcis and Eretria
journeys.sum: Euboean Greeks settle Pithekoussai (Ischia) and Cumae, the first Greek colonies in Italy.

Starting world c. 750 BC: the Aegean, the Hellespont and the entrance to the Black Sea, Sicily and southern Italy, Egypt and the Nile up to Thebes, Phoenicia (Sidon), Cyprus and the Libyan coast, as reflected in the Homeric poems and the first Euboean colonies.
Phoenician colony at Lixus on the Loukkos estuary, first foothold on Africa's Atlantic coast.
Phoenician settlements on Malta and at Motya, Panormus (Palermo) and Solus in western Sicily.
Greek colonies ring eastern and southern Sicily: Naxos, Syracuse, Gela, Akragas and Selinus.
Achaean and Spartan colonies at Sybaris, Croton and Taras round the Gulf of Taranto.
Megarians found Byzantium and Chalcedon at the Bosporus, the gateway to the Black Sea.
Settlement of Ebusus (Ibiza) in the Balearics, described as Carthage's first recorded independent action.
Phoenician trading station on Mogador Island (Essaouira), the southernmost known Phoenician site on the Atlantic.
A Samian trader driven west beyond the Pillars of Heracles reaches Tartessos, the first recorded Greek visit to Atlantic Spain.
Therans under Battus found Cyrene (inland of its port Apollonia), opening Greek knowledge of Libya.
Milesian colonies on the western and northern Black Sea: Apollonia, Istros, Tyras, Berezan and Olbia at the Dnieper-Bug estuary.
Milesians found Sinope on the southern Black Sea coast, base for Pontic expansion.
Greek trading post of Naucratis on the Canopic Nile, Greece's window on Egypt.

journeys.n: Spring and Autumn states of the Yangtze (base)
journeys.sum: The middle and lower Yangtze states of Chu, Wu and Yue as they entered the Chinese record.
Greek colonies in Crimea and the Kerch strait (Panticapaeum, Theodosia, Phanagoria), later the Bosporan kingdom.

journeys.n: Phoenician crews of Pharaoh Necho II
journeys.sum: Herodotus reports Phoenicians sent by Necho II sailed from the Red Sea round Libya (Africa) and back through the Pillars in three years.
Phocaeans found Massalia (Marseille) near the Rhone mouth, with Alalia on Corsica and later Elea.
Colonies along the eastern Black Sea at Amisos, Trapezus, Phasis in Colchis and Dioscurias.
Phocaeans found Emporion and trade down the Iberian coast to Tartessos, whose king Arganthonios befriended them.
A Massaliote voyage down Africa's Atlantic coast to a great crocodile-filled river, probably the Senegal.
A Carian Greek in Persian service sails down the Indus to the sea, the first Greek account of India.
Scylax sails west from the Indus mouth and round Arabia to Suez, 30 months in all.

World of Hecataeus' Periodos Ges c. 500 BC: a coastal circuit from the Pillars of Heracles clockwise round the Mediterranean and Black Sea to Atlantic Morocco, with Egypt and the Persian heartland along the Royal Road.
Carthaginian fleet of 60 ships founds colonies on Atlantic Morocco and sails down West Africa past the Senegal toward a burning mountain and the 'Gorillai'.
journeys.g: Interpreters from the Lixitae accompanied the fleet.

journeys.sum: Carthaginian voyage north along Atlantic Iberia to the tin lands of the Oestrymnides (Brittany), perhaps the British Isles.
Herodotus travels up the Nile to Elephantine and records Egypt and hearsay of Meroe and Nubia beyond.
Herodotus' travels in Syria and Mesopotamia, possibly to Babylon and Susa, describing the Persian empire.
Herodotus visits the Black Sea and the Scythian coast to the Borysthenes (Dnieper), gathering the first detailed account of the steppe peoples.

journeys.n: Cyrus the Younger and the Ten Thousand (Xenophon)
journeys.sum: The march of the Ten Thousand from Sardis through Cilicia and down the Euphrates to Cunaxa near Babylon.
Retreat of the Ten Thousand up the Tigris, through the Carduchian mountains and Armenian winter to the Black Sea at Trapezus.
journeys.g: Xenophon records local guides, including an Armenian village headman.

journeys.sum: The Ten Thousand move west along the Pontic coast by ship and on foot via Cotyora, Sinope and Heraclea to Byzantium.
Alexander's Balkan campaign across the Haemus to the Danube and into Illyria.
Alexander crosses to Asia, wins at the Granicus and Issus, takes Tyre and Gaza and enters Egypt, founding Alexandria and visiting Siwa.
Alexander marches across Mesopotamia to Gaugamela, takes Babylon, Susa and Persepolis, then Ecbatana.
Pursuit of Darius and Bessus through Parthia, Aria, Drangiana and Arachosia, over the Hindu Kush to Bactria and Sogdiana as far as the Jaxartes.
journeys.g: Local guides and rulers supplied routes over the Hindu Kush.

journeys.sum: Alexander crosses the Hindu Kush into the Kabul valley and Swat, crosses the Indus, defeats Porus on the Hydaspes and reaches the Hyphasis (Beas).
journeys.g: Taxiles of Taxila allied with Alexander and provided guides and elephants.

journeys.sum: Fleet and army descend the Hydaspes, Acesines and Indus to Patala and the Indus delta.
Return through the Gedrosian desert (Makran) and Carmania to Persepolis, Susa, Opis and Babylon.
Craterus leads the heavy troops and elephants from the Indus through the Bolan pass, Arachosia and Drangiana to Carmania.
Nearchus sails the fleet from the Indus along the Makran coast and up the Persian Gulf to the Tigris mouth, charting the route by sea.
journeys.g: A Gedrosian pilot, Hydraces, guided the fleet from Mosarna (Arrian, Indica).

journeys.sum: Pytheas sails from Massalia out of the Mediterranean, round Brittany and Britain and north to Thule, giving the first account of the British Isles and the Arctic north.
Pytheas visits the amber coast of northern Europe (Abalus) and the Guiones, perhaps turning back at the Vistula.
Seleucid envoy Megasthenes travels from Arachosia through the Punjab and down the Ganges plain to Pataliputra, writing the Indica.
Seleucid admiral Patrocles explores the Caspian Sea, wrongly concluding it was a gulf of the outer Ocean.
Bosporan Greek trading city of Tanais at the mouth of the Don, the edge of the Greek world toward the steppe.
Rome conquers the Po valley after Telamon, founding Placentia, Cremona, Bononia and Aquileia.
The unified Qin empire with Sichuan, Lingnan, Liaodong and the Ordos frontier of the Great Wall.

journeys.n: Gnaeus and Publius Cornelius Scipio, Scipio Africanus
journeys.sum: Roman armies land at Emporion and fight Carthage down eastern and southern Spain to Carthago Nova, Baecula, Ilipa and Gades.
Cato subdues Hispania Citerior north of the Ebro, marches into Turdetania and the Celtiberian interior at Segestica (Siguenza).
Gracchus campaigns in the Ebro valley and Celtiberian plateau, founding Gracchurris and making treaties with the Celtiberians.
Lucullus pushes west across the Duero plateau against the Vaccaei at Cauca, Intercatia and Pallantia, with Scipio Aemilianus serving under him.
After the fall of Carthage, Polybius explores Africa's Atlantic coast with a fleet lent by Scipio Aemilianus.
First Chinese envoy to the west: reached Dayuan (Ferghana), Kangju, the Yuezhi and Daxia (Bactria), and reported on Parthia and India.
journeys.g: Held by the Xiongnu for about ten years each way; accompanied by the Xiongnu-born guide Ganfu (Tangyi Fu).

journeys.sum: Han armies took the Hexi Corridor from the Xiongnu and founded the four commanderies to Dunhuang and the Jade Gate.
Embassy to the Wusun of the Ili and Issyk Kul region; his deputies went on to Dayuan, Kangju, the Yuezhi, Daxia, Anxi (Parthia) and Shendu.
Eudoxus, guided by a shipwrecked Indian sailor, sails from Egypt to India and back, and on a second voyage is blown down the Somali coast.
journeys.g: 118 BC with an Indian pilot; second 116 BC.

journeys.sum: First Greek voyage on the monsoon route straight across the Arabian Sea from the Red Sea to India.
journeys.g: Guided on the first voyage by a shipwrecked Indian sailor rescued in the Red Sea (Poseidonius via Strabo).

journeys.sum: Conquest of Nanyue added Lingnan, Hainan and the Red River delta, with Rinan commandery reaching central Vietnam.
Attempt to sail from Gades round Africa down the Atlantic coast of Morocco; turned back, a later attempt vanished.
Han armies took Wanggeom (Pyongyang) and set up the Four Commanderies including Lelang in north Korea.

journeys.n: Li Guangli (War of the Heavenly Horses)
journeys.sum: Han army crossed the Tarim and the Tian Shan to besiege Ershi, capital of Dayuan in the Ferghana valley.

journeys.n: Han envoys to Huangzhi (Book of Han)
journeys.sum: Book of Han itinerary from Rinan and Hepu along Indochina to Dulu and Huangzhi (probably Kanchipuram) and Yichengbu (Sri Lanka).
Roman army pursuing Mithridates crossed Armenia into Iberia and Albania (Georgia, Azerbaijan) and reached the Phasis, bringing the Caucasus into Roman knowledge.
Caesar's eight-year conquest mapped all of Gaul from the Alps to the Channel and the Rhine, with first-hand descriptions of Gaulish and German peoples.
First Roman crossing to Britain, landing on the Kent coast between Hythe and Sandwich.
Second invasion pushed inland across the Stour and the Thames to Cassivellaunus' stronghold, giving Rome its first description of inland Britain.
journeys.g: Guided partly by the Trinovantes under Mandubracius.

journeys.sum: Credited with the direct open-sea crossing to south India on the south-west monsoon, making Muziris a regular Roman port.
Roman army landed at Leuke Kome and marched six months down western Arabia to besiege Marib, bringing back the first Roman eyewitness geography of Arabia Felix.
journeys.g: Misled (Strabo says) by the Nabataean guide Syllaeus.

journeys.sum: Punitive campaign up the Nile through Lower Nubia to Napata, the Kushite royal city, after Kushite raids on Syene.
Campaign into the Fezzan that captured fifteen Garamantian settlements, the first Roman army deep in the Sahara.
Juba II's expedition to the Fortunate Isles (Canary Islands), reported by Pliny, put the Canaries on the Roman map.
First Roman fleet in the North Sea: down the Rhine and the Fossa Drusiana through Lake Flevo to the Frisian coast and the land of the Chauci.
Drusus marched from the Lippe to the Weser (11 BC) and from Mainz through the Chatti and Cherusci to the Elbe (9 BC), the furthest east any Roman army had gone in Germany.
Greek itinerary of caravan stations across the Parthian empire, from the Euphrates to Arachosia (Kandahar), possibly written for Augustus' grandson Gaius Caesar.
The Roman fleet sailed past the Elbe mouth up the coast of Jutland to the land of the Cimbri and the Skaw, glimpsing the Kattegat and the Baltic beyond.
Tiberius' army marched through the Chauci and Langobardi to the lower Elbe, where it met the fleet.
Germanicus moved his army by a fleet of about a thousand ships from the Rhine through Lake Flevo to the Ems before marching to the Weser; the fleet was wrecked by a North Sea storm on return.
First Roman army to cross the Atlas mountains, reaching the desert river Ger beyond; Pliny quotes his description.
Greek merchant's handbook describing every port down the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa to Rhapta on the Tanzanian coast, the furthest south Roman knowledge reached.
The Periplus describes the incense coast of Arabia, the Indus port of Barbarikon, Barygaza, the Malabar pepper ports of Muziris and Nelcynda, Roman-traded Poduke (Arikamedu) and the Ganges mouth.

journeys.n: Roman knight sent by Julianus (Nero's games)
journeys.sum: A Roman eques travelled from Carnuntum along the Amber Road to the Baltic coast to buy amber, as Pliny reports.
Party sent by Nero up the Nile past Meroe and up the White Nile to the impassable swamps of the Sudd.
journeys.g: Helped by the Kushite king of Meroe with guides and letters to rulers upstream.

journeys.sum: Thirty years restoring Han power over the Tarim kingdoms, from Shanshan and Khotan to Kashgar, Kucha and Karashahr.
Agricola's campaigns carried Roman armies through northern Britain beyond the Forth and Tay to the battle of Mons Graupius in north-east Scotland.
Agricola's fleet sailed round the north of Britain, proving it an island, subdued the Orkneys and sighted Thule (probably Shetland).
Roman commander who marched from Garama three months south into the land of the 'Ethiopians', as reported by Marinus of Tyre via Ptolemy.
Roman traveller who accompanied the Garamantian king four months south from Garama to Agisymba, a land of rhinoceroses, probably near Lake Chad.
Sent to reach Da Qin (Rome), he crossed Parthia to the sea at Tiaozhi (probably the head of the Persian Gulf) and turned back.

Agents of the Macedonian merchant Maes Titianus travelled the Silk Road from the Euphrates through Parthia and Bactria to the Stone Tower and on to Sera, the silk capital; their distances reached Ptolemy via Marinus of Tyre.
Trajan's Parthian war took a Roman army down the Tigris past Ctesiphon to Charax Spasinou and the Persian Gulf.
Ptolemy's Geography (c. 150) gave coordinates for some 8,000 places from Ireland and the Canaries to the Silk Road, India, Sri Lanka and the Golden Chersonese, summing up Roman knowledge.

journeys.n: Embassy of 'Andun' (Marcus Aurelius) to Han China
journeys.sum: Men claiming to come from the Roman emperor 'Andun' (Antoninus) reached China by sea through Rinan in central Vietnam, the first recorded direct Roman contact with China.

journeys.n: Embassy of 'Andun' (Marcus Aurelius) to Han China
journeys.sum: Overland stage of the 166 embassy from Rinan through Jiaozhi to the Han court at Luoyang, where it presented ivory, rhinoceros horn and tortoiseshell to Emperor Huan.

journeys.n: Wei envoys to the Wa (Weizhi Wajinden)
journeys.sum: Embassies between Daifang and Queen Himiko of Yamatai, giving the first Chinese itinerary to Tsushima, Iki and Kyushu.
Wu envoys to Funan in the Mekong delta, whose reports described Funan and lands as far as India.
Pilgrim Egeria's letters describe Sinai, the Holy Land, Mount Nebo, Edessa and Harran in detail for readers in the far west of Europe.
journeys.g: Guided by local monks and clergy at each holy site.

journeys.sum: Overland across the Taklamakan and the Pamirs to Gandhara and the Buddhist holy places of the Ganges, the first full Chinese account of India.
From Tamralipti to Sri Lanka (two years), then via Yepoti (Java or Sumatra) home to the Shandong coast at Laoshan.
Voyagers from southeast Borneo (Ma'anyan-related) settled Madagascar across the Indian Ocean, mixing with East Africans.

journeys.n: St Brendan of Clonfert (Navigatio Sancti Brendani)
journeys.sum: Legendary voyage of St Brendan to islands in the northern Ocean (perhaps the Hebrides, Faroes and Iceland), written down c. 900 and widely read in medieval Europe.
Alexandrian merchant whose Christian Topography (c. 550) describes Adulis, Aksum, Socotra, the pepper coast of Male and Taprobane (Sri Lanka) as a hub of Indian Ocean trade.
Byzantine envoy who travelled to the court of the Turkic khagan Istemi in the Tian Shan, and whose report described the steppe route north of the Caspian.

journeys.n: Arabia at the rise of Islam (base)
journeys.sum: The Arabian peninsula, its Red Sea and Gulf coasts and caravan towns, the home world of the first Muslim community.
Slipped out of Tang China, crossed the Tian Shan to the Western Turkic khagan at Suyab, then Samarkand, Balkh, Bamiyan and Gandhara to Kashmir.
Studied at Nalanda and travelled around India from Bengal and Kamarupa to Kanchipuram, the Deccan, Gujarat and Sind.

journeys.n: Rashidun conquests of Syria, Iraq and Egypt (base)
journeys.sum: Syria, Palestine, Mesopotamia and Egypt as conquered by the Rashidun armies between 634 and 642.
Tang envoy to King Harsha who used the new Tibet and Nepal road; in 648 he led Tibetan and Nepalese troops into north India.
Home over the Hindu Kush, Badakhshan, the Wakhan and the Pamirs to Kashgar and Khotan, reaching Chang'an in 645.
The former Sasanian lands of Iran, Khurasan and the Caucasus brought into the caliphate by 651.
Sailed from Guangzhou to Srivijaya (Palembang), Malayu and Kedah and across the Bay of Bengal to Tamralipti, recording the maritime Buddhist world.
Ifriqiya and the Maghreb to the Atlantic, conquered between the fall of Carthage (698) and about 710.
Irish hermits settled the Faroe Islands about a century before the Norse, as Dicuil records.
Most of the Iberian peninsula and Septimania (Narbonne, 719 to 759) under Umayyad rule.
Transoxiana (Bukhara, Samarkand, Ferghana) taken by Qutayba ibn Muslim and Sind to Multan by Muhammad ibn Qasim, 705 to 715.
Led a Tang army over the Pamirs and the Darkot pass to Little Balur (Gilgit) in 747, then west to defeat at Talas in 751.
Captured at Talas, he lived in the Abbasid world and his Jingxingji gave the first Chinese eyewitness description of the Arabs at Kufa.

journeys.n: Jia Dan (route from Guangzhou to the Arab lands)
journeys.sum: Tang geographer Jia Dan's itinerary of the sea route from Guangzhou through the Strait of Malacca, Sri Lanka and India to the Euphrates mouth and Baghdad.
Irish clerics lived in Thule (Iceland) from February to August 795 and sailed a day north to the frozen sea; Dicuil wrote it down in 825.
Charlemagne's embassy to Harun al-Rashid in Baghdad; the sole survivor Isaac returned via Ifriqiya with the elephant Abul-Abbas.

journeys.n: Varangian Rus' (route from the Varangians to the Greeks)
journeys.sum: Norse traders and warriors opened the river road from the Baltic by the Neva, Lake Ladoga, Novgorod and the Dnieper rapids to the Black Sea and Constantinople, attacked in 860.
First surviving Arabic account of the sea route from Siraf via Kulam Mali, the Nicobars, Kalah and Champa to Khanfu (Guangzhou).
Gardar sailed right round Iceland, proving it an island, and wintered at Husavik.
Norse sailor blown off course to the Faroes who reached east Iceland and named it Snaeland.
Floki followed his ravens to Iceland, wintered at Vatnsfjordur in the Westfjords and gave the island its name.

journeys.n: Ibn Khordadbeh (Book of Roads and Kingdoms)
journeys.sum: The Abbasid post road from Baghdad through Khurasan to Transoxiana and the Turkic steppe, with stages and distances.

journeys.n: Ibn Khordadbeh (sea route to China and al-Sila)
journeys.sum: First Arabic mention of al-Sila (Silla, Korea) at the far end of the sea route along the China coast.
The northern Radhanite trade route from the land of the Franks through the Slav lands and Khazar Itil to Transoxiana and China.
Seven days' sail from Hedeby to Truso at the Vistula mouth, describing the Wendish coast, the Danish and Swedish islands and the Aestii, recorded for King Alfred.
Earliest Arabic account of the Fezzan route from Zawila to Kanem near Lake Chad, also naming Kawkaw (Gao) and Ghana.
Ohthere sailed round the North Cape and along the Kola coast into the White Sea to the land of the Beormas, the first known account of the European Arctic coast.
Ohthere's month-long voyage down the Norwegian coast to the market at Skiringssal (Kaupang) and on to Hedeby, the first description of Norway as a long coastal land.
Storm-driven Norse sailor who sighted islands (Gunnbjarnarsker) off east Greenland, the first European sighting of Greenland.
Rus' fleets reached the Caspian Sea by the Volga (and the Don portage) and raided its coasts from Baku to Abaskun and Gorgan.
Voyage to Sind (Mansura, Multan), Cambay, Saymur and Ceylon described in Muruj al-Dhahab.
Sailed from Oman down the Somali and Zanj coast to Qanbalu (probably Pemba), the earliest firsthand Arabic account of the Swahili coast.

journeys.n: Swahili coast trade to Sofala (Arabic accounts)
journeys.sum: The gold and ivory trade of the Swahili towns (Zanzibar, Kilwa) reaching south to Sofala of the Zanj, as reported by al-Mas'udi.
Embassy from Baghdad via Bukhara and Khwarazm across the Oghuz steppe to the Volga Bulgars, with the famous description of the Rus.
Thirty years of travel (943 to 973) from Iraq across North Africa to al-Andalus and Sijilmasa, extending Arabic description to the Sahara edge.
Rus' fleet sailed down the west Caspian coast and up the Kura river to seize Barda, the capital of Arran.
Ahsan al-Taqasim (985), a systematic survey of every province of the Islamic world from personal travel.
During three years of exile Erik explored the south-west coast of Greenland and chose the fjords that became the Norse settlements.
Bjarni, blown off course sailing for Greenland, sighted three unknown lands to the west, the first recorded European sighting of North America.
The Eastern and Western Settlements of Norse Greenland and their summer hunting grounds (Nordrsetur) north to Disko Bay and Upernavik, where a runestone of c. 1300 was found.
Leif sailed to Helluland (Baffin Island), Markland (Labrador) and Vinland, wintering at Leifsbudir, probably in northern Newfoundland.
Polynesian voyagers sailed back west to settle Tuvalu and the Outliers such as Tikopia, Rennell, Ontong Java, Kapingamarangi and Nukuoro.
Karlsefni's attempt to settle Vinland with about 160 people explored south into the Gulf of St Lawrence (Straumfjord and Hop) before conflict with the Skraelings ended it.
Followed the Ghaznavid court to Ghazni and the Punjab; measured the earth at Nandana and learned Sanskrit for his Kitab al-Hind (1030).
The first settlement of East Polynesia, in the Society Islands (Tahiti, Raiatea), after the long pause in Samoa and Tonga.
Northern India from the Punjab to the Ganges and Malwa, described from Sanskrit learning in al-Biruni's India.
Large Swedish expedition east to Serkland (the Muslim lands round the Caspian) that ended in disaster in 1041, commemorated on some 26 Ingvar runestones.
Book of Roads and Kingdoms describing Awdaghust, Takrur, Silla, the royal town of Ghana, Kawkaw (Gao) and Tadmekka.
Adam of Bremen's history (c. 1075) described the Baltic, Sweden, Norway to Halogaland, the Gulf of Bothnia, Estonia, Iceland, Greenland and, for the first time in a European book, Vinland.

journeys.n: First Crusade (Godfrey of Bouillon and others)
journeys.sum: Crusader armies marched from the Rhineland down the Danube to Constantinople and across Anatolia to Antioch and Jerusalem, and their chronicles gave Western readers first-hand geography of Anatolia and Syria.
journeys.g: Guided across Anatolia by Byzantine troops under Tatikios and by Armenian Christians.

journeys.sum: Baldwin left the main army, crossed the Euphrates and took Edessa, founding the first crusader state in upper Mesopotamia.
Contact with the Pacific coast of South America, attested by the pre-Columbian sweet potato in Polynesia and by Native American DNA in East Polynesians.
The Sahel from Takrur to Kanem, Nubia, Abyssinia and the east African coast to Sofala as shown on the Tabula Rogeriana.
Western, northern and eastern Europe (Britain, Norway, the Baltic, Poland, Rus) charted for Roger II from informants at Palermo.
Benjamin's itinerary described some 300 cities from Spain through Italy, Greece, Constantinople, the Levant, Baghdad and Persia to Egypt, with hearsay of Arabia, India and China.
Sailed on a Genoese ship from Ceuta past Sardinia, Sicily and Crete to Alexandria in 1183.
Up the Nile and across the Red Sea to Mecca, then by the pilgrim caravan to Baghdad, Mosul, Aleppo, Damascus and Crusader Acre.
From Acre on a Christian ship, wrecked at Messina, through Norman Sicily to Cartagena in 1185.

journeys.n: Settlement of the Austral Islands and Rapa
journeys.sum: Settlement of Rurutu, Tubuai, Raivavae and remote Rapa Iti south of Tahiti.
Settlement of the southern Cook Islands (Aitutaki, Rarotonga, Mangaia) from the Society Islands.
Settlement of the Marquesas via the Tuamotus, later a hub for voyages to Hawaii and Rapa Nui.
Small Pitcairn and Henderson were settled from Mangareva and traded stone and shell with it.

journeys.n: Settlement of the Tuamotus and Mangareva
journeys.sum: Atolls of the Tuamotus and the high islands of Mangareva (Gambier), a gateway to Pitcairn and Rapa Nui.
Icelandic annals record 'Svalbard found' in 1194, a land four days' sail north of Iceland, probably Jan Mayen or the east coast of Greenland.
Settlement of Rapa Nui (Easter Island), the eastern apex of the Polynesian triangle.
Settlement of the Hawaiian Islands, probably from the Marquesas and later in contact with Tahiti (Kahiki).
Daoist master who crossed Mongolia, the Altai and the Tian Shan to Samarkand and met Genghis Khan in the Hindu Kush; recorded in Xiyou ji.
Song customs inspector Zhao Rugua described foreign lands from the Philippines and Java to India, Arabia, Zanzibar, Egypt, Sicily and the Maghreb.

journeys.n: Giovanni da Pian del Carpine (with Benedict the Pole)
journeys.sum: Franciscan envoy who crossed the steppe from Kiev via Batu's camp on the Volga to the Mongol court near Karakorum, writing the first European account of the Mongols and Inner Asia.
journeys.g: Benedict the Pole served as companion and interpreter; Mongol relay stations carried them.

journeys.sum: The last large land mass settled by humans, reached via the Kermadecs; earliest sites such as Wairau Bar date to the late 13th century.

Franciscan who travelled from Constantinople across the Crimea and steppe to Mongke Khan at Karakorum and back via Derbent and Armenia; his report first told Europe that the Caspian is a lake and that Cathay was the land of the Seres.
journeys.g: Relied on Mongol guides and an unreliable dragoman.

journeys.sum: Gave Europe its first detailed description of the Silk Road through Persia, the Pamirs, the Tarim Basin and the Hexi corridor to Kublai Khan's court.
Two Uyghur or Ongud monks from Khanbaliq crossed the Tarim and Khurasan to the Ilkhanate at Maragheh and Baghdad.
Described the interior of China from Khanbaliq to Yunnan and the Burmese border, and south through Hangzhou to Zaitun (Quanzhou).
First known person from China to reach western Europe: Constantinople, Naples, Rome, Genoa, Paris (Philip IV) and Gascony (Edward I).
Two Genoese galleys sailed out through the Strait of Gibraltar and down the Moroccan Atlantic coast seeking India by sea, and vanished.
Return overland from Hormuz through Persia to Tabriz and Trebizond on the Black Sea.
Yuan embassy from Wenzhou along the coast of Champa to the Mekong mouth; his Customs of Cambodia is the only eyewitness account of Angkor at its height.
Up the Mekong and Tonle Sap to Yasodharapura (Angkor), where he lived for about a year.

journeys.n: Polynesian visit to the Auckland Islands
journeys.sum: Southernmost known Polynesian site, on Enderby Island in the subantarctic Auckland Islands, about 465 km south of New Zealand.
Raoul Island, a stepping stone between East Polynesia and New Zealand, was briefly occupied.
Norfolk Island had a Polynesian settlement at Emily Bay, probably from the Kermadecs or New Zealand, abandoned before 1774.
Genoese navigator who reached Lanzarote, the first of the Canaries to reappear on a European map (Dulcert, 1339).
Crossed Armenia and Persia from Trebizond via Tabriz, Sultaniyeh, Kashan, Yazd and Persepolis to Hormuz.
Travelled from Canton and Zaitun up through Fuzhou, Hangzhou and Nanjing and the Grand Canal to Khanbaliq, giving Europe a vivid account of south China.
From Tangier along North Africa to Egypt, up the Nile to Aydhab, then through Palestine and Syria to Mecca.
With the returning Iraqi hajj caravan to Najaf and Basra, then Isfahan, Shiraz, Baghdad, Tabriz and Mosul.
Down the Red Sea to Aden and Zeila, along the Swahili coast to Mogadishu, Mombasa and Kilwa, then back via Dhofar, Oman, Hormuz and Bahrain.
Through Anatolia and across the Black Sea to the Golden Horde, to Constantinople and back, then via Khwarazm, Bukhara, Samarkand and Afghanistan to the Indus.
Two merchant voyages whose Daoyi Zhilue (1349) described about 100 places from Temasek (Singapore) to India, Hormuz and the Somali coast.
Sind and Multan to Delhi, where he served Muhammad bin Tughluq, then south through Malwa and Daulatabad to Cambay.
Papal embassy across the Golden Horde and Chagatai steppes via Sarai, Almaliq and Hami to Khanbaliq.

journeys.n: Niccoloso da Recco and Angiolino del Tegghia de Corbizzi
journeys.sum: Three-ship Portuguese-sponsored expedition that spent five months mapping thirteen islands of the Canaries.
Down the Malabar coast to Calicut, then the Maldives (where he served as qadi), Ceylon and Adam's Peak, Ma'bar and Bengal.
From Bengal via Samudra (Sumatra) and the South China Sea to Zaitun (Quanzhou) and Guangzhou.
Back from China via Sumatra, Quilon and Calicut across the Arabian Sea to Dhofar and Hormuz.
Through Iran, Iraq and Syria during the Black Death to a last hajj at Mecca, then Cairo and Alexandria before sailing west to Fez (1349).
Across the strait to Gibraltar, Ronda, Malaga and Nasrid Granada.
Across the Sahara via Taghaza and Walata to the capital of Mali, then Timbuktu, Gao and Takedda and back north via Tuwat.

journeys.n: Jean de Bethencourt and Gadifer de La Salle
journeys.sum: Norman conquest of Lanzarote, Fuerteventura and El Hierro, described in the chronicle Le Canarien.
Castilian embassy to Timur, describing the road from Trebizond through Persia and Khorasan to Samarkand.
A Toulousain said to have lived eight years at Gao on the Niger and returned with an African wife, but his writings had no effect on European maps.
Treasure fleet to Champa, Java, Palembang, Malacca, Semudera, Ceylon and Calicut.
Second fleet visited Siam as well as Java, Malacca, Ceylon, Cochin and Calicut.
Third voyage to Calicut; on the way home the fleet fought and captured the king of Kotte in Ceylon (1411).
First fleet beyond India, reaching Hormuz at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
journeys.g: Ma Huan, Muslim interpreter, sailed on this voyage and wrote Yingya Shenglan.

journeys.sum: Ming embassy to Shahrukh at Herat via Turfan, the Ili, Tashkent and Samarkand; recorded in Xiyu Fanguo Zhi.
Fleet and detachments reached Hormuz, Aden and the east African ports of Mogadishu, Brava and Malindi.

journeys.n: Joao Goncalves Zarco, Tristao Vaz Teixeira, Bartolomeu Perestrelo
journeys.sum: Portuguese caravels recognised Porto Santo and then Madeira, settled from 1425.
Crossed the Syrian desert from Damascus to Baghdad and went down the Tigris to Basra.
Went inland from Cambay to the city of Vijayanagar and across the peninsula to Mylapore.
Returned foreign envoys home; detachments visited Dhofar, Aden, Mogadishu and Brava.
From Bengal to Arakan and overland to Ava and Pegu, the first European account of Burma's interior.
Portuguese pilot credited with finding the eastern and possibly central Azores.
Found the Formigas rocks and Santa Maria, beginning the official Portuguese discovery of the Azores.
Last voyage to Hormuz; a detachment with Ma Huan sailed up the Red Sea to Jeddah for Mecca.
First recorded European ship to pass Cape Bojador and return, opening the Saharan coast.

journeys.n: Gil Eanes and Afonso Goncalves Baldaia
journeys.sum: Sailed 30 to 50 leagues beyond Bojador to the bay they named Angra dos Ruivos.
Named the Rio do Ouro inlet (Dakhla) and crossed the Tropic of Cancer to Pedra da Gale off Cape Barbas.
Reached Cape Blanc (Ras Nouadhibou).
Reached the Bay of Arguin and Arguin island.
Reached the Langue de Barbarie near the mouth of the Senegal River, the edge of the Sahel.
Passed Cap Vert to a large river, probably in the Sine-Saloum delta, where he was killed.
Genoese merchant whose 1447 letter from the Tuat oasis gave Europe its first eyewitness report of the Sahara trade and hearsay of Timbuktu and the Niger.
Moriori ancestors from New Zealand settled the Chatham Islands, 800 km east of the mainland.
Venetian in Henry's service who described Senegal, Cayor and the Gambia mouth in his widely printed Navigazioni.
Reported the Cape Verde Islands (Boa Vista, Santiago), went up the Gambia to Badibu and on to the Geba estuary and Bissagos.
Sailed about 60 Italian miles up the Gambia to visit the ruler he called Battimansa in Badibu.
Reached the Rio Grande (Geba) and then sailed some 50 leagues up the Gambia to the Mali gold market of Cantor.
Went about 50 leagues up the Gambia to Cantor, a market town for Mali gold.

journeys.n: Diogo Gomes and Antonio de Noli
journeys.sum: Traded in the Saloum delta and landed on and named Santiago in the Cape Verde Islands.
Kitab al-Fawa'id (c. 1490), a pilot's manual of Indian Ocean sea routes, star altitudes and coasts from the Gulf to Malacca.
Charted the coast of Sierra Leone and Liberia past Cape Mount and Cape Mesurado to the Bosco de Santa Maria.
journeys.g: Turned back because his interpreters could not understand the local language.

journeys.sum: From Tver down the Volga, round the Caspian and across Persia to Hormuz, the first Russian account of the route to India.
Described the Deccan interior: Junnar, the Bahmani capital Bidar and the shrine of Parvattum.
First European to reach Bioko (Formosa, later Fernando Po) and the Cameroon coast at the head of the Gulf of Guinea.
Returned from Hormuz across Persia and eastern Anatolia to Trebizond, then from Caffa north towards Smolensk, where he died.
Found the mouth of the Congo and followed the Angolan coast to Cabo de Santa Maria, setting stone padroes.
Second voyage carrying the coast survey on to Cabo Negro and Cape Cross in Namibia.
Portuguese boats ascended the Congo estuary to the Yellala falls, leaving a carved inscription, the first European penetration of the river.

journeys.n: Pero da Covilha and Afonso de Paiva
journeys.sum: Royal spies sent to find the spice routes and Prester John crossed Egypt from Alexandria via Cairo to the Red Sea.
Travelling on Arab and Indian trading vessels he saw Aden, Calicut, Goa, Hormuz and the Swahili coast to Sofala, reporting the Indian Ocean trade to Lisbon.
Rounded the southern tip of Africa unseen, landed at Mossel Bay, reached Kwaaihoek and sighted the Cape of Good Hope on the way home.
Portuguese embassy marched from Mpinda at the Congo mouth to the Kongo capital Mbanza Kongo, opening the kingdom to European description.
First European crossing to the Bahamas, Cuba and Hispaniola, opening the Caribbean to European knowledge.
journeys.g: Landfall at Guanahani (San Salvador, identification debated); Taino captives taken as interpreters.

journeys.sum: Portuguese envoy who, after scouting Cairo, Aden, India and Sofala, went inland from Zeila to the Ethiopian court and never left.
After revisiting Aden, Hormuz and Jeddah he crossed the Red Sea from Sinai to Zeila on the Somali coast.
Charted the Lesser Antilles, Puerto Rico, Jamaica and the south coast of Cuba.
Went inland from Zeila to the court of the Ethiopian emperor Eskender, where he spent the rest of his life.
English landfall in Newfoundland, the first recorded European visit to mainland North America since the Norse.
First sea voyage from Europe to India, charting the Natal and Swahili coasts and crossing the Arabian Sea to Calicut.
journeys.g: At Malindi he took on a Gujarati pilot who knew the monsoon route.

journeys.sum: First European sighting of the South American mainland at Trinidad, the Gulf of Paria and the Orinoco outflow.

journeys.n: Alonso de Ojeda, Juan de la Cosa, Amerigo Vespucci
journeys.sum: Followed the Venezuelan coast from the Orinoco to the Guajira, naming the Gulf of Venezuela and Lake Maracaibo.
First European landfall in Brazil and first entry into the Amazon estuary, the 'Mar Dulce'.
Second India fleet: made the first recorded European landfall in Brazil (Monte Pascoal, Porto Seguro), then reached Sofala, Kilwa, Calicut and Cochin.
Separated from Cabral, he sighted Madagascar (Sao Lourenco), sailed past Cape Guardafui into the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea mouth.
Followed the Brazilian coast south to Rio de Janeiro and Cananeia, convincing Vespucci it was a new continent.
Third India fleet, credited with finding Ascension on the way out and St Helena on the way home.
Coasted Central America from Honduras to Panama, adding the Caribbean shore of the isthmus to the map.

journeys.n: Estevao da Gama's squadron of Vasco da Gama's 4th India fleet (account by Thome Lopes)
journeys.sum: Eyewitness account of the 1502 to 1503 India voyage, describing St Helena as an unknown island on 30 July 1503 and mentioning Ascension.
Sailed alone by the outer route east of Madagascar to Cape Guardafui and became the first Portuguese to reach and winter on Socotra.
First known non-Muslim European to describe Medina and Mecca, travelling with the Damascus Hajj caravan, then explored Yemen from Aden to Sanaa.
Travelled inland from Hormuz to Herat and Shiraz with a Persian merchant partner.
Sighted the remote South Atlantic islands that bear his name, then raided the Swahili coast and took Socotra.
Sent by Tristao da Cunha to explore around Madagascar, he found Reunion (Santa Apolonia), Mauritius (Cirne) and Rodrigues.
Followed the Omani coast from Ras al Hadd via Qalhat, Muscat and Sohar into the Persian Gulf to Hormuz.
First Portuguese fleet to reach Malacca, after calling on Sumatra's northern ports.
His Description of Africa, written in Italy and printed by Ramusio in 1550, shaped European knowledge of Timbuktu and the Sahel for centuries.

journeys.n: Antonio de Abreu and Francisco Serrao
journeys.sum: First European fleet to the Banda Islands, following the north coast of Java and the Lesser Sunda chain.
Captured Malacca, from which embassies and fleets went to Siam, Pegu, the Spice Islands and China.
A Portuguese degredado who walked inland from Sofala to Manica and the Mutapa state, the first European report of the Zimbabwe plateau.
Shipwrecked survivors rescued by local rulers were taken into the Moluccas, where Serrao stayed and sent news of the clove islands.
First European fleet in the Red Sea; failed to take Aden and reached Kamaran island.
First Portuguese to reach China by sea, landing at Tamao in the Pearl River delta.
First Europeans to see the Pacific from the Americas, after crossing the Isthmus of Darien.
journeys.g: Relied on Indigenous guides and more than 1,000 native bearers; reached the Gulf of San Miguel.

journeys.sum: Ottoman world map compiled from Portuguese, Spanish and Columbus charts, showing the Atlantic, West Africa, Brazil and the Caribbean.
First recorded European exploration of Florida's Atlantic coast, Keys and Gulf coast.
journeys.g: Pilot Anton de Alaminos discovered the Gulf Stream on this voyage (general knowledge).

journeys.sum: Discovered the Rio de la Plata estuary, opening the way to the Parana and Uruguay rivers.

journeys.n: Fernao Pires de Andrade (with Tome Pires)
journeys.sum: First official Portuguese mission to China, sailing up the Pearl River to Canton.
First European expedition to the Maya coast of Yucatan, reaching Campeche and Champoton.
journeys.g: Two Maya fishermen seized at Cabo Catoche became interpreters.

journeys.sum: Followed the Gulf coast of Mexico from Cozumel past Tabasco to Veracruz, bringing first news of the Aztec state.
March from the Gulf coast to Tenochtitlan, revealing the Valley of Mexico and the Aztec capital to Europe.
journeys.g: Interpreters Malintzin (Dona Marina) and Geronimo de Aguilar; Totonac and Tlaxcalan allies guided and fought alongside.

journeys.sum: Charted the Patagonian coast and found the strait to the Pacific (Atlantic and strait leg only).
First map of the whole northern Gulf of Mexico coast, from Florida to Veracruz, including the Mississippi mouth.

journeys.n: Francisco Álvares (embassy of Rodrigo de Lima)
journeys.sum: Six-year Portuguese embassy to Lebna Dengel whose printed narrative (1540) gave Europe the first detailed descriptions of Aksum and Lalibela.
First European crossing of the Pacific, revealing its width, the Marianas and the Philippines, and reaching the Moluccas from the east.
journeys.g: Survivors guided in the Philippines by Malay interpreter Enrique.

journeys.sum: Governor's Red Sea campaign that landed the first official Portuguese embassy to Ethiopia.
Failed attempt by the Trinidad to sail back east across the North Pacific, reaching about 42 or 43 degrees N before scurvy forced a return.
Conquest route into highland Guatemala and Cuzcatlan (El Salvador).
Overland march across Tabasco and the Peten to Honduras, crossing the Maya lowlands.
Surveyed the coast from Florida to Nova Scotia for Spain, ascending the Penobscot and naming the Hudson the Rio de San Antonio.
First survey of the North American Atlantic coast from the Carolinas to Newfoundland, including New York Bay.

journeys.n: Garcia Jofre de Loaisa; Toribio Alonso de Salazar
journeys.sum: Second Spanish fleet through the Strait of Magellan; its flagship crossed the Pacific via Bokak atoll and Guam to Mindanao and the Moluccas.

journeys.n: Francisco Pizarro, Diego de Almagro, Bartolome Ruiz
journeys.sum: Sailed down the Pacific coast of Colombia and Ecuador to Tumbes, the first European contact with the Inca state.
First crossing from Mexico to the Moluccas; its return attempts ran along the north coast of New Guinea to the Admiralties and Marshalls.
Eight-year odyssey of four survivors across Texas and northern Mexico, the first European account of the region.
Overland march through northern Florida to Apalachee, then raft voyage along the Gulf coast to Texas.
Conquest route from Tumbes to Cajamarca and along the Inca road to Cusco, opening the Andes to Europe.
journeys.g: Interpreters Felipillo and Martinillo, taken at Tumbes earlier.

journeys.sum: From Piura to Quito, then north through the Cauca valley to Popayan, Cali and the Bogota plateau.
Mapped the Gulf of St Lawrence, Prince Edward Island, Chaleur Bay and Gaspe.
journeys.g: Took Domagaya and Taignoagny, sons of the Stadacona chief Donnacona, who later guided him upriver.

journeys.sum: First European expedition into Chile, via the Altiplano and northwest Argentina over the Andes to Copiapo and the Itata.
journeys.g: Thousands of Andean auxiliaries; guide Paullu Inca accompanied.

journeys.sum: Ascended the St Lawrence to Stadacona (Quebec) and Hochelaga (Montreal); returned by the Cabot Strait.
journeys.g: Guided by Domagaya and Taignoagny; Domagaya's remedy (annedda) saved the crew from scurvy.

journeys.sum: Crossed the Venezuelan and Colombian llanos along the foot of the Andes and climbed to Bogota.
Up the Magdalena and onto the Muisca highlands, revealing the Bogota plateau, Tunja and Sogamoso.
Adventurer whose Peregrinacao (1614) gave Europe a sweeping, if embroidered, picture of the Red Sea, Malacca, Siam, Pegu, China and Japan.

journeys.n: Hernando de Soto (then Luis de Moscoso)
journeys.sum: Four-year march across the American Southeast, crossing the Mississippi and reaching east Texas.
journeys.g: Juan Ortiz, a Narvaez survivor, interpreted.

journeys.sum: Showed Baja California to be a peninsula by sailing to the head of the Gulf of California and round to Cedros Island.
First Europeans at the Grand Canyon, reaching the South Rim near Desert View.
journeys.g: Led there by Hopi guides; Pedro de Sotomayor chronicled.

journeys.n: Joao de Castro (in Estevao da Gama's fleet)
journeys.sum: Expedition to Suez whose Roteiro do Mar Roxo was the first detailed European survey of the Red Sea coasts, with charts and views.
Searched for Cibola and Quivira, revealing the Pueblo world, the Llano Estacado and the Great Plains as far as Kansas.
journeys.g: Guided onto the Plains by the captive known as El Turco and by Ysopete (Wichita).

journeys.sum: Marched through the Atacama to found Santiago, then pushed south to Concepcion, Valdivia and Villarrica.

journeys.n: Cristóvão da Gama (account by Miguel de Castanhoso)
journeys.sum: Portuguese musketeers marched from Massawa through Tigray to Lake Tana's battlefields; Castanhoso's account (1564) described the highlands.
First descent of the Amazon from the Napo to the Atlantic, naming the Rio Negro.
First European voyage along the coast of Alta California, from San Diego Bay to near Point Reyes.
Crossed from New Spain to Mindanao and named the islands Filipinas; Inigo Ortiz de Retes then followed the north coast of New Guinea and named it Nueva Guinea (1545).

journeys.n: Antonio Mota and Francisco Zeimoto (Portuguese traders)
journeys.sum: First Europeans to reach Japan, landing on Tanegashima and introducing firearms.
Naval reconnaissance of the Chilean coast south of Valparaiso to about 41 S.
Jesuit mission that landed at Kagoshima, beginning the Jesuit letters that described Japan to Europe.
journeys.g: Guided and interpreted by the Japanese convert Anjiro.

journeys.sum: Took the Ottoman Basra squadron out of the Gulf; after battles with the Portuguese off Oman and a storm it was wrecked on the Gujarat coast.
Mirat ul-Memalik: overland from Gujarat through Sind, Mughal Delhi, Kabul, Transoxiana and Safavid Iran back to Istanbul.
Englishman who went down the Volga, across the Caspian and the Ustyurt desert via Urgench to Bukhara; his 1562 map of Russia and Tartary followed.

journeys.n: Pedro de Ursua, Lope de Aguirre
journeys.sum: Descent of the Huallaga, Maranon and Amazon in search of Omagua and El Dorado, ending in Aguirre's revolt in Venezuela.
Crossing from New Spain via the Marshalls and Guam to Samar and Cebu, founding the Spanish Philippines.

journeys.n: Andres de Urdaneta; Felipe de Salcedo
journeys.sum: The tornaviaje: first west to east crossing of the Pacific, via the westerlies near 38 N, opening the Manila galleon route.
Discovered the Solomon Islands (Santa Isabel, Guadalcanal, Malaita, Makira) and returned via the Marshalls and Wake to Mexico.
Portuguese army ascended the Zambezi to Sena and campaigned inland, establishing the river route into Mutapa lands.

journeys.n: Portuguese Macau to Nagasaki trade ship (nau do trato)
journeys.sum: Portuguese helped found the port of Nagasaki with daimyo Omura Sumitada, the terminus of annual ships from Macau.
Entered Frobisher Bay on Baffin Island (1576 to 1578) and in 1578 sailed some way into Hudson Strait.
Cossack raid over the Urals by the Chusovaya, Tagil, Tura and Tobol to Qashliq, capital of the Khanate of Sibir, opening western Siberia to Russia.
Dutch secretary to the Archbishop of Goa whose Itinerario (1596) published Portuguese sailing directions to the East.
Charted south-west Greenland and Cumberland Sound, and in 1587 sailed up Davis Strait to 72 12 N (Hope Sanderson).
Return voyage via St Helena and two years on Terceira in the Azores before reaching Lisbon and Enkhuizen.
First English voyage to the Indian Ocean, via Zanzibar and Cape Comorin to Penang and Ceylon.
First Dutch voyage to the East Indies, reaching Bantam, the north Java coast, Madura and Bali.

journeys.n: Alvaro de Mendana; Pedro Fernandes de Queiros
journeys.sum: Discovered the Marquesas and the Santa Cruz Islands; after Mendana's death Queiros took the survivors to Manila.
Ascended the Orinoco via the Manamo channel to the Caroni, producing 'The Discovery of Guiana'.
journeys.g: Chief Topiawari supplied information and guides; his son went to England.

journeys.sum: Discovered Bear Island and Spitsbergen, rounded the north of Novaya Zemlya and survived the first Arctic wintering, escaping by open boat to Kola.
Zeeland voyage to Aceh where Cornelis was killed and Frederick imprisoned, later publishing a Malay-Dutch dictionary and southern star catalogue.
Second Dutch fleet; van Neck's ships resupplied on Madagascar's east coast and loaded spices at Bantam.
Part of the second Dutch fleet that landed on and named Mauritius, then sailed via Ambon to Ternate.
Reached Great Banda and left 22 men to buy nutmeg, the first Dutch post in the Bandas.
Brought the first Dutch ships to the China coast, at Macau, where Portuguese forces killed his landing parties.
First East India Company fleet: Table Bay, Antongil Bay in Madagascar, the Nicobars, Aceh, Priaman and Bantam, where the first English factory was set up.
Overland from Agra via Kabul, the Pamirs, Yarkand and the Tarim towns to Suzhou (Jiuquan), proving that Cathay was China.
Re-examined the St Lawrence from Tadoussac to the Lachine rapids.
Spanish Jesuit who settled at Gorgora on Lake Tana and on 21 April 1618 visited the springs of the Blue Nile at Gish Abay.

journeys.n: Samuel de Champlain, Pierre Dugua de Mons
journeys.sum: Surveyed the Bay of Fundy and the coast of Maine and Massachusetts as far as Cape Cod.
Dutch merchant whose journal of trading voyages to Cape Verde, Guinea and Angola was published in 1634.
First recorded European landfall on Australia, charting the west coast of Cape York in the Gulf of Carpentaria.
Searched for Terra Australis, crossing the Tuamotus to Taumako and Espiritu Santo (Vanuatu), then returned to Acapulco.
Sailed west along the south coast of New Guinea and through Torres Strait, proving New Guinea was not part of a southern continent.
Sought a polar route: in 1607 along east Greenland to Spitsbergen at 80 N (finding Jan Mayen area waters), in 1608 to Novaya Zemlya.
Up the Richelieu to the lake later named Lake Champlain.
journeys.g: Travelled with Wendat, Algonquin and Montagnais allies, who guided the war party.

journeys.sum: Ascended the Hudson River to near Albany, laying the basis for New Netherland.
Passed through Hudson Strait into Hudson Bay and down the east coast to James Bay.
Crossed Hudson Bay to winter at the Nelson River, then charted the west coast north to about 65 N.
First Dutch merchant in Arabia, at Aden and al-Shihr in Hadramawt, where Dutch traders were left to learn Arabic.
Explored Foxe Channel along Southampton Island, showing no western outlet from Hudson Bay.
Via the Ottawa River and Lake Nipissing to Georgian Bay and Huronia, then across Lake Ontario into Iroquois country.
journeys.g: Wendat guides; Etienne Brule had gone ahead.

journeys.sum: Circuited Baffin Bay, finding Smith, Jones and Lancaster sounds and reaching 77 45 N.
Portuguese trader who walked from Tete past the south end of Lake Malawi to Kilwa on the Swahili coast.
Tried to open a Dutch post at Mocha (where he tasted coffee), then founded the VOC establishment at Surat.
Landed on Dirk Hartog Island and charted the Western Australian coast north to about 22 S (Eendrachtsland).
Opened the Le Maire Strait and Cape Horn route and crossed the Pacific via the Tuamotus, northern Tonga and Futuna to New Ireland and New Guinea.
Danish expedition through Hudson Strait to winter at the Churchill River mouth on Hudson Bay; only three survived.
First Russians to reach the Lena, going up the Lower Tunguska and down the Lena towards the site of Yakutsk, returning by the Angara.
Charted the south coast of New Guinea (sighting its snow peaks) and the east side of the Gulf of Carpentaria to the Staaten River.

journeys.n: Antonio de Andrade and Manuel Marques
journeys.sum: First Europeans known to enter Tibet, crossing the Mana Pass to Tsaparang, capital of Guge.
Jesuit who crossed the Danakil from Beilul to Tigray, visited the Blue Nile source in 1629 and left via Massawa; his account reached Europe in French (1728) and Johnson's English (1735).
First Europeans in Bhutan, continuing over the Himalaya to Shigatse in central Tibet.
Charted about 1,500 km of the southern coast of Australia from Cape Leeuwin to the Nuyts Archipelago.
From Yeniseysk up the Angara and Ilim, over the portage to the Lena, and down it to found the Yakutsk ostrog in 1632.
First European ascent of the whole Amazon, to Quito, and back; Cristobal de Acuna's account followed.
First Russians to reach the Pacific, by the Aldan, Maya and Ulya rivers to the Sea of Okhotsk.
journeys.g: Guided over the Dzhugdzhur by Evenki knowledge.

journeys.sum: Sailed up the Vitim to the Tsipa, the first Russian to enter Transbaikalia (Dauria).
Down the Indigirka to the Arctic and east along the coast to the Kolyma, where the first ostrog was built.
Discovered Van Diemen's Land (Tasmania), the west coast of New Zealand, Tonga and Fiji, proving Australia did not join a southern continent.
First Russian descent of the Amur: up the Aldan and Gonam, over the Stanovoy range, down the Zeya and Amur to its mouth, then along the Okhotsk coast and back by the Maya.
Charted the north coast of Australia from Cape York round the Gulf of Carpentaria and Arnhem Land to the north-west coast, as one continuous New Holland.
Sailed from the Kolyma round the eastern tip of Asia through the strait later named for Bering, proving Asia and America were separated.
Survivors walked from the wreck to the Anadyr mouth and went upriver to found winter quarters near Anadyrsk.
Bandeira from Sao Paulo across the Paraguay basin to the Andes foothills and down the Madeira and Amazon.
Up the Olyokma and Tungir to the Shilka and Amur, built Albazin and sailed down the Amur past the Sungari to near modern Khabarovsk.
Opened the overland route from the Kolyma via the Anyuy to the Anadyr, then reached the Penzhina and followed the north coast of the Sea of Okhotsk to Okhotsk.

journeys.n: Hendrick Hamel and the Sperwer crew
journeys.sum: Shipwrecked Dutch sailors held in Korea for 13 years; Hamel's journal was Europe's first first-hand account of Joseon Korea.
Peking to Agra by Xining, the Kokonor and Lhasa, then over the Himalaya to Kathmandu, the first Europeans in Lhasa.
Accompanied Kara Mehmed Pasha's embassy to Vienna and described the Habsburg capital in the Seyahatname.
Travelled up the Nile through Ottoman Egypt and Nubia towards the Funj sultanate of Sennar.
Down the Fox-Wisconsin route and the Mississippi to the Arkansas mouth, proving the river drains to the Gulf.
journeys.g: Five voyageurs; Miami and Illinois guides on the Fox-Wisconsin portage.

journeys.sum: First sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes, through Lakes Erie, Huron and Michigan to Green Bay.
Descended the Illinois and Mississippi to the Gulf of Mexico and claimed Louisiana for France.
First systematic Russian exploration of Kamchatka, from Anadyrsk down both coasts and the Kamchatka river to the Golygina.
journeys.g: Party included about 60 Yukaghirs; Itelmen allies guided them on the Kamchatka.

journeys.sum: Surveyed Shark Bay and the north-west coast of Australia, then found New Britain and the strait between it and New Guinea.
Qing embassy across Mongolia and Siberia to Ayuka Khan of the Kalmyks on the lower Volga; described in Yiyu lu (1723).
Delhi to Kashmir, Ladakh and across western Tibet past Kailash to Lhasa, followed by the fullest early European study of Tibet.

journeys.n: Kangxi atlas survey (Huangyu Quanlan Tu, base-like)
journeys.sum: Jesuit and Chinese survey of the whole Qing realm (1708 to 1717), with lama surveyors mapping Tibet to Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar.
First scientific expedition through Siberia, from Tobolsk via Tomsk, the Yenisei and Lower Tunguska to Irkutsk and Dauria.
Qing armies from Kokonor and Sichuan expelled the Dzungars and occupied Lhasa.
Left Lhasa by Kuti on the Nepal border and returned via the Ganges plain to Agra.
Found Easter Island (5 April 1722), islands of the Tuamotus and Society group (Bora Bora, Maupiti) and Samoa.
First Kamchatka Expedition: sailed north along Kamchatka and Chukotka through the Bering Strait to 67 18 N.

journeys.n: Johann Georg Gmelin and Gerhard Friedrich Muller
journeys.sp: Russian Academy of Sciences (Great Northern Expedition)
journeys.sum: Academic land party of the Great Northern Expedition, surveying western and southern Siberia, Baikal and Dauria before reaching Yakutsk.

journeys.n: Murillo Velarde map of the Philippines
journeys.sum: The first scientific map of the Philippines, 1734.

journeys.n: Jesuit surveyors for the Kangxi Emperor (Regis, Jartoux, Fridelli and others)
journeys.sum: The Jesuit-Qing triangulation survey of China, Manchuria and Korea (1708-1718) reached European readers through Du Halde (1735) and d'Anville's atlas, replacing guesswork with measured maps.
Western detachment of the Great Northern Expedition: charted the Kara Sea coast from the Pechora past Yamal to the Ob estuary.

journeys.sp: Russian Academy of Sciences (Great Northern Expedition)
journeys.sum: Spent four years exploring Kamchatka; his Description of Kamchatka (1755) was Europe's first full account of the peninsula and its Itelmen people.

journeys.n: Jesuit survey of China, published by d'Anville
journeys.sum: The Kangxi survey by Jesuits and Chinese surveyors (1708 to 1717), published in Europe in d'Anville's atlas of 1737.
From Fort La Reine to the Mandan villages on the upper Missouri.
journeys.g: Assiniboine guides.

journeys.sum: Charted the Arctic coast from the Lena delta past the Indigirka to the Kolyma, then went overland to the Anadyr.
Sailed the Laptev Sea coast from the Lena to the Khatanga Gulf; his sledge survey of the Taymyr is included in chelyuskin-1742.
journeys.g: Mixed ship and sledge survey; relied on Evenk and Dolgan guides and reindeer transport.

journeys.sum: Second Kamchatka Expedition: first European sighting of north-west America (Mount Saint Elias, Kayak Island) and of the Aleutian chain.
Sledge surveys of the Taymyr Peninsula: Khariton Laptev along the west coast (1741) and Chelyuskin to Cape Chelyuskin, the northernmost point of Eurasia (May 1742).
Reached the Alexander Archipelago of southeast Alaska, the first European sighting of the Northwest Coast there.
First Europeans on the northern Great Plains west of the Missouri, sighting the Rockies (probably the Bighorns).
journeys.g: Two Mandan guides; travelled with Bow People war party.

journeys.sum: First scientific map of the Amazon, descending from the Maranon through the Pongo de Manseriche to Para.
The settled coast and the gold country of Minas Gerais, mapped for the Treaty of Madrid (1750).
First European to reach the Alberta plains and meet the Blackfoot, near present Red Deer.
journeys.g: Cree companions; Attickasish interpreted.

journeys.n: Qing conquest of Dzungaria and the Tarim
journeys.sum: Qing conquest of the Dzungar Khanate and Altishahr, followed by Jesuit-assisted surveys of the new territory.
The settled colonies from New England to Georgia, mapped in detail on John Mitchell's map of 1755.
Scientific expedition that mapped Yemen from the Tihama to Sanaa; Niebuhr was its only survivor.
Fast circumnavigation crossing the Tuamotus (Disappointment Islands), Tokelau and Kiribati (Nikunau) to Tinian.
Overland return from the Gulf via Shiraz and Persepolis (where he copied cuneiform), Babylon, Baghdad, Mosul and Aleppo to Constantinople.

journeys.n: Murray map of the St Lawrence; Maritime colonies
journeys.sum: The settled St Lawrence valley, surveyed for the Murray map of 1761 to 1763, and the Maritime colonies.
Discovered Pitcairn Island and St George's Channel, separating New Ireland from New Britain.
First European visit to Tahiti (June 1767), adding the Tuamotus, Society Islands and Uvea (Wallis Island).
First French circumnavigation: Tahiti, Samoa, northern Vanuatu, the Great Barrier Reef edge, the Louisiades and the Solomons (Bougainville Island).
Reached Gondar in 1770 and the Blue Nile springs at Gish Abay, then returned via Sennar and the Nubian desert; his Travels (1790) mapped Abyssinia and the Blue Nile.
Observed the Transit of Venus at Tahiti, charted the whole of New Zealand and the east coast of Australia, and passed through Torres Strait.
journeys.g: Tahitian navigator Tupaia joined at Tahiti and mediated with Maori in New Zealand.

journeys.sum: First European overland journey to the Arctic coast, at the Coppermine mouth, and first to cross Great Slave Lake.
journeys.g: Guided by the Chipewyan leader Matonabbee, whose party (including his wives) did much of the work.

journeys.sum: James Cook's survey of Newfoundland, 1763 to 1767, published by 1770.
Search for Terra Australis from Mauritius that discovered the Kerguelen Islands in the southern Indian Ocean.
First crossing of the Antarctic Circle (17 January 1773) and a long sweep of the high southern latitudes, then Tahiti and Tonga.
Reached 71 10 S, then charted Easter Island, the Marquesas, Vanuatu, New Caledonia and Norfolk Island, and returned via South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands.
Second expedition (Roland and Oiseau) revisited Kerguelen and showed the islands barren, ending hopes of a southern continent there.
Attempt on the North Pole via Spitsbergen, blocked by ice at about 80 48 N near the Seven Islands.
Warren Hastings' envoy through Bhutan to the Panchen Lama near Shigatse, the first British mission to Tibet.

journeys.n: Andean Spanish America, Cruz Cano map of South America
journeys.sum: The Andean highlands and Pacific coast of the viceroyalties, mapped on Cruz Cano's map of 1775.
The settled Central Valley of Chile.

journeys.n: Spanish colonial America, Cruz Cano map
journeys.sum: The settled colonial cores of Central America and the Caribbean.
Third voyage outward leg: Tasmania, New Zealand, the Cook Islands, Tonga, Tubuai, Tahiti, Kiritimati and the first European landfall in Hawaii.
Charted the Northwest Coast from Oregon to Nootka, Prince William Sound, Cook Inlet and the Aleutians.
Charted the north-west coast of America from Oregon to the Bering Strait, reached Icy Cape at 70 N, and after Cook's death Clerke probed the Arctic again from Kamchatka.

journeys.n: Jean-Francois de Galaup, comte de La Perouse
journeys.sum: Pacific crossing via Easter Island and Maui to the Alaska coast (Lituya Bay), south to Monterey and across to the Marianas and Manila.

journeys.n: Jean-Francois de Galaup, comte de La Perouse
journeys.sum: Explored the Sea of Japan, the Tartary coast and the strait now named for him, then via Kamchatka, Samoa and Botany Bay to his wreck at Vanikoro.
Open-boat voyage after the Bounty mutiny, from Tofua through Fiji and the Banks Islands to Timor, sketching coasts along the way.
Descended the Mackenzie River from Great Slave Lake to the Arctic Ocean.
journeys.g: Guided by the Chipewyan leader known as English Chief; Dene guides along the river.

journeys.n: Early United States: Kentucky, Tennessee, Vermont, Maine
journeys.sum: Settled and surveyed by the first federal census of 1790.
Survey from Cumberland House to Lake Athabasca and Great Slave Lake, fixing positions for the first accurate maps.
Spanish scientific expedition's survey of Yakutat Bay, Prince William Sound, Nootka and Monterey.
Pacific legs: King George Sound in south-west Australia, Dusky Sound, the Snares, Rapa, Tahiti and Hawaii, before his survey of the North American coast.
Searching for La Perouse, charted south-east Tasmania, New Caledonia, the Solomons and Louisiades, the south coast of Australia and the north coast of New Guinea.
First recorded crossing of North America north of Mexico, via the Peace and Fraser rivers to the Pacific at Dean Channel.
journeys.g: Followed the Nuxalk-Dakelh grease trail with Indigenous guides.

journeys.sum: Detailed survey of the Northwest Coast from California to Cook Inlet, including Puget Sound and the Inside Passage.
From Pisania on the Gambia through Kaarta and Ludamar to the Niger at Ségou (21 July 1796), proving it flows east, then back by a more southerly route.
journeys.g: Set out with two local guides; nursed for seven months at Kamalia by the trader Karfa Taura.

journeys.sum: Circumnavigated Van Diemen's Land, proving Bass Strait separates Tasmania from the mainland.
German in British service who crossed from Cairo via Siwa and Awjila to Murzuk in Fezzan, the first European there in modern times.
Portuguese expedition from Tete to the court of the Kazembe south of Lake Mweru, where Lacerda died; his diary mapped the route.
Proved the Casiquiare links the Orinoco and Amazon basins; first scientific mapping of the upper Orinoco.
journeys.g: Indigenous pilots and Capuchin missionaries guided the canoes.

journeys.sum: Settled and mapped by the end of the colonial period.

journeys.n: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata
journeys.sum: The settled provinces of the viceroyalty and the Banda Oriental (Uruguay).
The General Land Survey begun in 1765 mapped the provinces of European Russia.
The Public Land Survey began with the Seven Ranges in 1785; Ohio was largely surveyed by 1800.
Charted much of the west, south (Terre Napoleon) and Tasmanian coasts, with major natural history and ethnographic collections.
First circumnavigation of Australia, charting the south coast and the Gulf of Carpentaria and popularising the name Australia.
Magdalena, Bogota, Quito and Chimborazo to Lima: founded the science of Andean geography and plant zones.

journeys.n: Pedro João Baptista and Amaro José (pombeiros)
journeys.sum: Two Afro-Portuguese trading agents made the first recorded crossing of south-central Africa, from Kasanje in Angola via the Lunda and Kazembe to Tete.
Survey of New Spain from Acapulco to Mexico City, Guanajuato and Veracruz, basis of his Political Essay.
Up the Missouri, over the Lemhi and Lolo passes and down the Snake and Columbia to the Pacific.
journeys.g: Sacagawea (Lemhi Shoshone) and Toussaint Charbonneau interpreted; Shoshone guide Old Toby led them over the Bitterroots; York, enslaved by Clark, was a full member.

journeys.sum: Descended the Niger in the boat Joliba from Sansanding past Timbuktu and Gao to the Bussa rapids, where he drowned; the river's lower course remained unknown.
journeys.g: Guide Isaaco carried Park's last letters back; Amadi Fatouma's later testimony is the only account of the river voyage, so the knowledge that reached Europe was partial.

journeys.sum: Return by the Yellowstone River, the first European descent of it.
journeys.g: Sacagawea guided the party to Bozeman Pass.

journeys.sum: Lambton's triangulation from the 1802 Madras baseline across the peninsula to Mangalore and down to Cape Comorin fixed south India accurately.
Return across the Continental Divide by the Blackfoot River and up the Marias.
journeys.g: Nez Perce guides showed the shortcut to the Great Falls.

journeys.sum: Up the Arkansas to the Colorado Rockies (Pikes Peak), then taken by Spanish troops through Santa Fe and Chihuahua.
Descended the Fraser River through its canyons to the Strait of Georgia.
journeys.g: Relied on Secwepemc, Nlaka'pamux and Sto:lo guides and their ladders and trails in the canyon.

journeys.sum: The French savants' survey of the Nile valley, published from 1809.

journeys.n: Felix de Azara, Voyages dans l'Amerique meridionale
journeys.sum: Azara's twenty years of survey in Paraguay, published in Paris in 1809.
First Englishman to reach Lhasa, where he met the young 9th Dalai Lama.

journeys.n: Humboldt, Political Essay on the Kingdom of New Spain
journeys.sum: Humboldt's essay and atlas (1811) summed up three centuries of colonial survey of Mexico.
Crossed Athabasca Pass and became the first European to travel the whole Columbia to its mouth.
Travelling as Sheikh Ibrahim, he reached Petra, the first European to see it since the Crusades, then crossed Sinai to Cairo.

journeys.n: Gregory Blaxland; William Lawson; William Charles Wentworth
journeys.sum: First recorded European crossing of the Blue Mountains west of Sydney, opening the inland plains.
Travelled up the Nile through Nubia to near the Third Cataract and on the way back found the sand-buried temple of Abu Simbel.
Crossed the Nubian desert to Berber and Shendi near Meroë, then to Taka and Suakin on the Red Sea, describing the Sudanese Nile towns.
Made the Hajj and gave Europe the first accurate descriptions of Mecca and Medina.

journeys.l: Public Land Survey: Gulf and Indiana
journeys.n: US Public Land Survey: Indiana, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama
journeys.sum: Surveyed townships and settlement across the Old Northwest and the Gulf states.
Discovered Kotzebue Sound in Alaska and charted the Ratak chain of the Marshall Islands in detail.
journeys.g: Marshallese navigator Kadu sailed with the Rurik and supplied island knowledge.

journeys.sum: Traced the Lachlan and Macquarie rivers into the inland marshes, then crossed the Liverpool Plains and the Great Dividing Range to Port Macquarie.

journeys.n: Johann Baptist von Spix, Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius
journeys.sum: Crossed Brazil from Rio to Bahia, Maranhao and Belem, then up the Amazon to its upper reaches.
Raffles's survey of Java, published with its map in 1817.
Re-surveyed Baffin Bay, met the Inughuit of the Thule region, and turned back in Lancaster Sound believing it closed by mountains.
journeys.g: Greenlandic interpreter John Sakeouse (Hans Zakaeus) enabled contact with the Inughuit.

journeys.n: Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen; Mikhail Lazarev
journeys.sum: First Russian Antarctic expedition: sighted the Antarctic ice shelf on 28 January 1820 and later Peter I Island and Alexander I Land, also charting Tuamotu islands.

journeys.n: John Franklin; John Richardson; George Back
journeys.sum: Overland to the Coppermine River mouth and east along the Arctic coast to Point Turnagain; disastrous starvation on the return.
journeys.g: Depended on Akaitcho and the Yellowknives Dene, and Inuit interpreters Tattannoeuck (Augustus) and Hoeootoerock (Junius).

journeys.sum: Sailed through Lancaster Sound and Barrow Strait to winter at Melville Island, more than halfway through the Northwest Passage.
First European to cross the Arabian peninsula, from the Gulf coast to Medina and Yanbu, chasing Ibrahim Pasha's army.
Accompanied Ismail Pasha's conquest of the Sudan, describing Meroë's pyramids and the Blue Nile up to Fazogli; published as Voyage à Méroé (1826).
Explored Ladakh and Kashmir, then crossed the Hindu Kush to Bukhara; Moorcroft died at Andkhoy.
Southern Ontario surveyed into townships for Loyalist and later settlement.
The western Cape, settled since 1652.
Mapped after the British conquest of Kandy in 1815.

journeys.n: Hugh Clapperton, Dixon Denham and Walter Oudney
journeys.sum: First Europeans to cross the Sahara from Tripoli to Bornu, reaching Lake Chad (4 Feb 1823) and Kukawa.
Clapperton went west through Kano to Sultan Bello's Sokoto, the first European description of the Hausa states and the Sokoto Caliphate.
Joined a raid into the Mandara mountains and surveyed the western and southern shores of Lake Chad and the lower Logone and Shari.
Sealer sailed into the sea now named for him, reaching 74 15 S in an unusually open season.
Overland from New South Wales to Port Phillip, finding the upper Murray (named the Hume) and good grazing country.
From Badagry through Yoruba country, across the Niger at Bussa and on to Kano and Sokoto, where Clapperton died in April 1827.
Second Arctic land expedition: down the Mackenzie and west along the Alaskan coast to Return Reef, while Richardson charted east to the Coppermine.
journeys.g: Interpreter Tattannoeuck (Augustus) again served.

journeys.sum: First European known to reach Timbuktu (Aug 1826), via Ghadames, In Salah and the Tanezrouft; he was killed on leaving and his papers were lost.

journeys.l: Public Land Survey: Illinois and Missouri
journeys.n: US Public Land Survey: Illinois, Missouri
journeys.sum: Statehood (1818, 1821) followed the township survey.
Charted New Zealand's coasts, Tonga, Fiji, the Loyalty Islands, New Britain and northern New Guinea, and found La Perouse's wreck at Vanikoro.
Canoe expedition from Sao Paulo via the Tiete, Pardo and Paraguay to Cuiaba, then down the Arinos, Juruena and Tapajos.
Disguised as a Muslim, walked from the Rio Nunez via Djenné to Timbuktu (April 1828) and was the first European to return alive, crossing the Sahara to Morocco.
Followed the Macquarie beyond its marshes and found the Darling River.
Steam vessel Victory explored Prince Regent Inlet and the Gulf of Boothia, wintering four times at Felix Harbour on Boothia.
Rowed down the Murrumbidgee and the Murray, past the Darling junction, to Lake Alexandrina, revealing the great inland river system.
Third circumnavigation of Antarctica; sighted Enderby Land (1831) and Adelaide Island and the Biscoe Islands off Graham Land (1832).
Sledged across Boothia to the north-west coast of King William Island (1830) and reached the North Magnetic Pole on the Boothia coast (1 June 1831).
journeys.g: Guided by Netsilik Inuit who drew coastline maps for the Rosses.

journeys.sum: Followed the lower Niger from Bussa to the delta, proving that Park's river reaches the Gulf of Guinea.
Settled and surveyed by the 1830s.
Portuguese expedition from Tete through Chewa and Bisa country to the Kazembe; Gamitto's O Muata Cazembe (1854) described the region.
Hydrographic survey of the coasts of Argentina, Tierra del Fuego and Chile, with Darwin's natural history.
Travels into Bokhara: from Lahore over the Hindu Kush to Bukhara and back through Merv and Persia.
Boat party up the Santa Cruz River to within sight of the Andes.

journeys.l: Public Land Survey: Michigan and Arkansas
journeys.n: US Public Land Survey: Michigan, Arkansas
journeys.sum: Township survey and settlement before statehood in 1836 and 1837.
Australia Felix expedition: the Lachlan and Murray, then south-west across western Victoria to the Grampians, Glenelg and Portland Bay.
journeys.g: Relied on Aboriginal guides including Piper and Turandurey (Kalkanjai).

journeys.sum: Charted Joinville Island and Louis Philippe Land (1838) and discovered Adelie Land, landing near Point Geologie (January 1840).
United States Exploring Expedition sailed west along some 2,400 km of the East Antarctic coast, establishing that Antarctica is a continent.
First east to west crossing along the Great Australian Bight (Nullarbor coast) from Fowlers Bay to Albany, after probing Lake Torrens to Mount Hopeless.
Broke through the pack into the Ross Sea, charting Victoria Land, Ross Island volcanoes and the Great Ice Barrier, and reached 78 10 S in 1842.
The Great Arc meridian survey from Cape Comorin to the Himalayan foothills near Mussoorie, the spine of the survey of India.
Surveyed the Oregon Trail to South Pass and the Wind River Range.
journeys.g: Guide Kit Carson; cartographer Charles Preuss.

journeys.sum: Great loop to Oregon, across the Great Basin (which he named), over the Sierra in winter and back via Utah.
journeys.g: Guides Kit Carson and Thomas Fitzpatrick; Washo and Paiute guidance at Pyramid Lake and the Sierra.

journeys.sum: Lazarist missionaries crossed Mongolia, the Ordos and Kokonor to Lhasa, then were escorted out to Sichuan.
Overland from the Darling Downs to Port Essington, opening the Dawson, Burdekin, Mitchell and Roper river country and the southern Gulf of Carpentaria.
journeys.g: Aboriginal guides Charley Fisher and Harry Brown.

journeys.sum: Central Australian expedition via the Darling and Depot Glen into the Strzelecki and Sturt Stony deserts, reaching the edge of the Simpson Desert.
Last Franklin expedition: circled Cornwallis Island, wintered at Beechey Island and was beset off King William Island, where all 129 men died.
British anti-slavery traveller who visited Ghadames, Ghat and Murzuk, describing the central Saharan caravan towns.

journeys.l: Public Land Survey: Iowa, Wisconsin, Florida
journeys.n: US Public Land Survey: Iowa, Wisconsin, Florida
journeys.sum: Surveyed and settled by statehood in 1845 to 1848.
The Great Journey: 550 days down the Buller River and the West Coast to near Paringa, finding the Grey valley and the Brunner coalfield.
journeys.g: Guided by Kehu (Ngati Tumatakokiri / Ngati Apa), with Pitewate and their wives.

journeys.sum: Attempted to traverse Cape York Peninsula from Rockingham Bay; most of the party died.
journeys.g: Only the Aboriginal guide Jackey Jackey (Galmahra) reached the relief ship; Kennedy was killed near the Escape River.

journeys.sum: German missionary who saw snow on Kilimanjaro in May 1848, a report doubted in London but later confirmed.
Slovene missionary who ascended the White Nile to Gondokoro, following the Egyptian river expeditions of 1839 to 1842.
Walked from Rabai to Kitui in Ukambani and was the first European to see Mount Kenya (Dec 1849).

journeys.n: David Livingstone (with William Cotton Oswell and Mungo Murray)
journeys.sum: Crossed the Kalahari from Kolobeng to Lake Ngami.
journeys.g: Route along the Boteti river from Nchokotsa; guided by Tswana.

journeys.n: Heinrich Barth, James Richardson and Adolf Overweg
journeys.sum: British-sponsored mission across the Sahara via Ghat and Aïr to Agadez (Oct 1850), Kano and Bornu.
Entered from Bering Strait, found Prince of Wales Strait and was trapped at Mercy Bay on Banks Island; completed the first transit of the passage partly on foot.
Settler frontier of the Eastern Cape and the Colony of Natal (1843).

journeys.n: Colonial surveys of New South Wales and Victoria
journeys.sum: Squatting runs and colonial surveys across the south east.
First European in Adamawa, reaching the upper Benue near Yola.

journeys.n: David Livingstone and William Cotton Oswell
journeys.sum: Reached the upper Zambezi at Sesheke in Kololo country (Aug 1851), revealing a great river in the heart of the continent.
Sailed the boat carried across the Sahara around Lake Chad and its Buduma islands, the first European navigation of the lake.
Visited Bagirmi (1852), then went west through Sokoto and across the Niger at Say to Timbuktu (Sept 1853).
Disguised as a pilgrim, went from Yanbu to Medina and by the eastern caravan road to Mecca.
Went up the Barotse valley and across the Kasai watershed to Luanda (May 1854), with 27 Kololo companions.
Sent to reinforce Barth; explored Bauchi and the Benue, then was killed entering Wadai in 1856.
Mapped the Niger bend between Timbuktu and Say, passing Gao, then returned to Tripoli via Bornu and Bilma (Sept 1855).
Disguised as an Arab merchant, Burton was the first European to enter Harar (3 Jan 1855), returning via Berbera.
Followed the Zambezi from Linyanti past Victoria Falls (Nov 1855) to Tete and Quelimane, completing the first recorded European coast-to-coast crossing of southern Africa.
