Settler colonisation, the Gold Rush and state surveys.
North Australian Expedition from the Victoria River to Sturt Creek and Lake Gregory, then east across the Gulf country to Brisbane.

journeys.n: Andrew Waugh and Survey of India computers
journeys.sum: Peaks of the Himalaya, including Peak XV (Everest) and Kangchenjunga, fixed from stations on the plains, since Nepal and Tibet were closed.

journeys.n: Richard Francis Burton and John Hanning Speke
journeys.sum: Followed the Arab caravan route from the coast via Kazeh (Tabora) to Ujiji, the first Europeans to see Lake Tanganyika (Feb 1858).
journeys.g: Guide and caravan leader Sidi Mubarak Bombay.

journeys.n: David Livingstone (Zambezi Expedition, with John Kirk)
journeys.sum: Steamed up the Zambezi to the Cahora Bassa rapids and up the Shire to Lake Chilwa and Lake Malawi, then boated up the lake's west shore.
Popularised Angkor in Europe and travelled from Bangkok via Korat to Luang Prabang, where he died.
Detoured north from Kazeh and reached Lake Victoria at Mwanza (30 July or 3 Aug 1858), guessing it was the Nile's source.
journeys.g: Bombay was his interpreter.

journeys.sum: Young Frenchman who lived among the Kel Ajjer Tuareg, visiting El Golea, Ghadames and Ghat; Les Touareg du Nord (1864) was the first study of them.

journeys.n: Robert O'Hara Burke; William John Wills
journeys.sum: First south to north crossing of Australia from Melbourne via Menindee and Cooper Creek to the tidal Flinders River near the Gulf of Carpentaria.

journeys.n: John Hanning Speke and James Augustus Grant
journeys.sum: Via Karagwe and Buganda to Ripon Falls, where the Nile leaves Lake Victoria (28 July 1862), then down through Bunyoro to Gondokoro and Khartoum.
The settled north mapped by the French army after 1830 (Tunisia after 1881).

journeys.l: Public Land Survey: Minnesota and Oregon
journeys.n: US Public Land Survey: Minnesota, Oregon, Washington
journeys.sum: Township survey under the Donation Land Claim Act and statehood.
Spent a year exploring the Atbara, Setit, Rahad and Dinder, the Ethiopian tributaries that bring the Nile flood.
First successful south to north crossing through the centre, from Chambers Creek to Chambers Bay near Darwin; the route of the Overland Telegraph.
From Gondokoro through Latuka and Bunyoro to Lake Albert (14 March 1864) and Murchison Falls, adding the second great Nile lake.
Crossed northern and central Arabia from Ma'an via Jawf, Hail and Riyadh to Hofuf and the Gulf.
Dutch traveller's expedition up the Bahr el Ghazal to Meshra er-Rek and overland toward the Azande country.
Disguised as a dervish, crossed the Turkmen desert to Khiva, Bukhara and Samarkand and returned via Herat.
Montgomerie's Kashmir and Karakoram triangulation (1855-1864) mapped the western Himalaya and fixed K2.
Counting paces with a rosary, the pundit fixed Lhasa's position and surveyed the Tsangpo trade route from Nepal to Lhasa and west to Manasarovar.
First European crossing from the Mediterranean to the Gulf of Guinea, via Bornu, Bauchi and the Benue confluence to Lagos.

journeys.n: Ernest Doudart de Lagree and Francis Garnier
journeys.sum: French Mekong Commission traced the river from Cambodia through Laos to Yunnan, showing it was unnavigable, then descended the Yangtze to Shanghai.
From the Rovuma round Lake Malawi to Lakes Mweru and Bangweulu and the Lualaba at Nyangwe, dying at Chitambo's village in 1873.

journeys.n: Nain Singh, Mani Singh and Kalian Singh (Pundits)
journeys.sum: Reached the Thok Jalung goldfields of western Tibet and mapped the upper Sutlej and Gartok.
Explored the Ussuri basin, Lake Khanka and the Pacific coast of the newly annexed Primorye.
As governor of Equatoria for the Khedive, Baker extended Egyptian rule south from Gondokoro to Bunyoro (Masindi).
First European to enter the Tibesti mountains, reaching Bardai.
First descent of the Green and Colorado rivers through the Grand Canyon, filling the last large blank in the US map.
Botanist who went via the Bahr el Ghazal through Bongo and Azande country to the Mangbetu and found the Uele flowing west, a river of the Congo basin.
From Bornu to Kanem, Borku, Bagirmi, Wadai, Darfur and Kordofan to Khartoum, the first European to traverse the eastern Sudan belt.
Crossed the Gobi to Peking, explored the Ordos and Alashan, the Kokonor and Tsaidam, and reached the upper Yangtze in northern Tibet.
journeys.g: Mongol and Tangut guides; intermediate points reconstructed.

journeys.n: Great Trigonometrical Survey and Atlas of India
journeys.sum: The triangulation of India and the sheets of the Atlas of India.
Siebold's Nippon (1832 to 1852) and Ino Tadataka's survey, copied by the British Admiralty in the 1860s.
Surveyed for settlement and land purchase by the 1870s.

journeys.l: Public Land Survey: Plains and Great Basin
journeys.n: US Public Land Survey: Kansas, Nebraska, Colorado, Utah, Nevada
journeys.sum: Surveyed for homesteading after 1862.
Marched from the coast via Tabora to Ujiji, found Livingstone (10 Nov 1871), and with him explored the north end of Lake Tanganyika.
Austro-Hungarian Tegetthoff drifted in pack ice to discover Franz Josef Land; Payer sledged north to Cape Fligely at 81 50 N.
First European to cross equatorial Africa from sea to sea, surveying Lake Tanganyika and its Lukuga outlet and following the Congo-Zambezi watershed to Benguela.
Scientific expedition from Dakhla into the Great Sand Sea, turning north to Siwa.
First crossing of the Great Sandy Desert by camel, from Alice Springs to the Oakover River and Roebourne.
West to east crossing from Geraldton through the Gibson Desert margin to the Overland Telegraph Line.
Crossed the northern Changtang lakes from Ladakh to Lhasa, then south through Tawang to Assam, revealing a vast unknown plateau.

journeys.sp: UK and USA (Daily Telegraph, New York Herald)
journeys.sum: Circumnavigated Lakes Victoria and Tanganyika, then followed the Lualaba from Nyangwe to the Atlantic, proving it was the Congo (Boma, 9 Aug 1877).

journeys.n: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza (with Noël Ballay and Alfred Marche)
journeys.sum: Ascended the Ogooué to its headwaters and crossed to the Alima, a Congo tributary.
Camel crossing of the Great Victoria Desert from South Australia via Queen Victoria Spring to Perth.
British Arctic Expedition pushed ships up Smith Sound and Kennedy and Robeson channels; Markham's sledge party reached 83 20 N.

journeys.sp: Italy (private; New South Wales steam launch)
journeys.sum: Steamed hundreds of kilometres up the Fly River aboard the Neva, the deepest European penetration of New Guinea at the time.
Travels in Arabia Deserta: Mada'in Salih, Tayma, Hail, Khaybar and Unaizah, the classic account of the Najd Bedouin.
As Gordon's officer, made missions from Lado to Buganda and Bunyoro, describing their courts and natural history.
Up the Rio Negro and Limay to Lake Nahuel Huapi.
journeys.g: Tehuelche and Mapuche hosts and guides.

journeys.sum: Surveyed north-western Mongolia from Zaysan to Kobdo, Hami and Uliastai.
Reached Lop Nur and the Altyn-Tagh from Kulja via the Yulduz and the lower Tarim.
Explored the upper Kwango and the Yaka country between Bié and Luanda.
Up the Santa Cruz River to the lake he named Lago Argentino, and onward to Lago Viedma.
Crossed from Benguela via Bié and the upper Zambezi to Victoria Falls and Pretoria.

journeys.n: Kishen Singh (Krishna Singh Rawat, Pundit A-K)
journeys.sum: Four-year pundit journey from Darjeeling through Lhasa to the Tsaidam and Dunhuang, returning across the Mekong, Salween and Irrawaddy headwaters.
First complete transit of the Northeast Passage, rounding Cape Chelyuskin and wintering on the Chukchi coast before passing Bering Strait.
First European to reach the Kufra oases in the Libyan desert (1879).
Explored the Uele and Ubangi watershed among the Azande and Mangbetu, then escaped Mahdist Sudan via Bunyoro, Buganda and Zanzibar.
First trans-Saharan expedition from Morocco via Tindouf and Taoudenni to Timbuktu and on to Senegal.
Via Hami and the Tsaidam to within about 260 km of Lhasa before being turned back, then explored the upper Yellow River.
Took over when Johnston died and reached Lakes Nyasa and Tanganyika, the Lukuga outlet and Lake Rukwa.
Crossed from Franceville to the Batéké kingdom, signed the Makoko treaty and founded the post at Stanley Pool that became Brazzaville.
French railway survey toward the Ahaggar, annihilated by Kel Ahaggar Tuareg at Bir el-Gharama (Feb 1881).

journeys.n: Colonial surveys of South Australia, Queensland and Western Australia
journeys.sum: The pastoral and agricultural south of each colony.

journeys.n: Orange Free State, Transvaal and Northern Cape
journeys.sum: Settled and surveyed into farms by the 1880s.

journeys.n: Survey of India: Punjab and Sindh
journeys.sum: Revenue and topographic survey after annexation (1843, 1849).
Crossed Africa from Luanda via the Kasai and Lulua to Nyangwe and Tabora to the east coast.

journeys.n: Nikolay Przhevalsky, Vsevolod Roborovsky and Pyotr Kozlov
journeys.sum: Reached the sources of the Yellow River, then went west along the Kunlun to Khotan and north to Lake Issyk-Kul.
First European through Maasai country from the coast to Lake Victoria, via Naivasha, Baringo and Mount Elgon.
Crossed from Moçâmedes via the upper Zambezi and Katanga (Msiri's Garanganja) to Tete and Quelimane, backing Portugal's pink-map claim.
From Peking across the Ordos to Lanzhou and Xining, south over the eastern Tibetan plateau to Songpan and back, wintering at Kumbum.

journeys.n: Argentine survey after the Conquest of the Desert
journeys.sum: Surveyed and settled after the campaigns of 1878 to 1885.

journeys.n: Southern British Columbia after the railway
journeys.sum: The railway belt and settled south of the province.

journeys.n: US Public Land Survey and USGS: Dakotas, Montana, Wyoming, Idaho, New Mexico, Arizona
journeys.sum: Township survey and the early topographic work of the US Geological Survey (founded 1879).
From the Niger via Sikasso, Kong, Bobo-Dioulasso and Ouagadougou to Salaga and the Ivory Coast, proving the 'Mountains of Kong' did not exist.
Pavie Mission surveyed Laos and the Tai uplands from Luang Prabang across to Hanoi, laying the basis for French Indochina's maps.

journeys.n: Henry Morton Stanley (Emin Pasha Relief Expedition)
journeys.sp: Britain (relief committee) and Congo Free State
journeys.sum: Up the Congo and Aruwimi and through the Ituri forest to Lake Albert, then south past the Ruwenzori and Lake Edward to the east coast.

journeys.n: Sámuel Teleki and Ludwig von Höhnel
journeys.sum: Via Kilimanjaro and Mount Kenya to Lake Rudolf (Turkana) and Lake Stefanie, the last large East African lakes unknown to Europe.
Peking to India across the Gobi and the Tarim towns, then over the Mustagh Pass in the Karakoram to Kashmir.
journeys.g: Guided across the Gobi by Liu San; Balti guide Wali over the Mustagh.

journeys.sum: First crossing of the Greenland ice sheet, from Umivik on the east coast to Ameralik fjord and Godthab.
Led Przhevalsky's last expedition after his death, surveying the Kunlun front, Niya, Lop Nur and the Turfan depression.
German expedition from the coast via Bukoba and the Lake Albert region into the Ituri, ending with Emin's murder near Kinena (Oct 1892).
French officer who marched from Ségou to Say, Sokoto, Kano and Bornu, then crossed the Sahara to Tripoli.

journeys.n: Dominion Land Survey of the prairies
journeys.sum: The prairies surveyed into sections for homesteading from 1871.
Crossed the north Greenland ice sheet to Independence Fjord (Navy Cliff), indicating Greenland's northern limit.
Fram drifted with the pack ice across the Arctic Ocean from the New Siberian Islands to north of Spitsbergen, proving there was no polar continent.
Nearly died crossing the Taklamakan, then found the buried cities of Dandan-Uiliq and crossed to Lop Nur, Tsaidam and Peking.
Canoed up the Ogooué beyond Lambaréné and crossed Fang country to the Rembwe, describing the region in Travels in West Africa (1897).
journeys.g: Local people acted as her porters and guides.

journeys.sum: Left the Fram to reach a Farthest North of 86 13.6 N, then retreated to winter on Franz Josef Land before meeting Jackson at Cape Flora.

journeys.n: Mission Pavie and the French survey of Indochina
journeys.sum: The Pavie Mission (1879 to 1895) and colonial survey.
Surveyed for the land runs of 1889 to 1895.
Crossed from the Loango coast via the Ubangi and Bahr el Ghazal to Fashoda on the White Nile (July 1898), then out through Ethiopia to Djibouti.
First wintering on the Antarctic mainland at Cape Adare, and first landing and sledge journey on the Great Ice Barrier (78 50 S).
Charted the Gerlache Strait and then made the first wintering south of the Antarctic Circle, beset in the Bellingshausen Sea.
First French military crossing of the Sahara, from Ouargla via the Aïr and Zinder to Lake Chad (Kousseri, 1900); Foureau continued down the Shari, Ubangi and Congo to the Atlantic.
Second Fram expedition: from Jones Sound, sledge parties discovered and mapped Axel Heiberg, Ellef Ringnes and Amund Ringnes islands.
Mapped the Tarim by boat, discovered the ruins of Loulan and crossed the Changtang towards Lhasa before being turned back.
Mongolia-Kham expedition through the Gobi Altai and Tsaidam into eastern Tibet.
Archaeological survey of the southern Tarim: Khotan, Dandan-Uiliq and Niya.
Surveyed after annexation in 1885.
Surveyed for settlement after 1890.

journeys.n: Robert Falcon Scott; Ernest Shackleton; Edward Wilson
journeys.sum: Discovery expedition: southern sledge journey to 82 17 S along the Barrier, and the 1903 western journey up the Ferrar Glacier onto the polar plateau.
First complete navigation of the Northwest Passage by a single ship, wintering at Gjoa Haven on King William Island.
Mapped by the French after annexation in 1896.
The railway (1891 to 1916) and the resettlement surveys that settled millions in southern Siberia.
Boundary survey of the Bolivia-Brazil-Peru frontier in the Acre and Abuna region.
Crossed the Transhimalaya repeatedly, visited Shigatse and traced the sources of the Brahmaputra, Indus and Sutlej.
Second expedition: Miran, the Lop desert, the Dunhuang library cave and the Gansu Nan Shan, with Survey of India mapping.
Discovered the Tangut city of Khara-Khoto in the Gobi and explored Amdo.
Telegraph-line surveys across Mato Grosso and Rondonia from Cuiaba to the Madeira.

journeys.n: Edgeworth David; Douglas Mawson; Alistair Mackay
journeys.sum: Northern Party man-hauled up the Victoria Land coast and across the plateau to the South Magnetic Pole.
Southern journey pioneered the Beardmore Glacier route and reached 88 23 S, 180 km from the South Pole.
Claimed sledge journey from Cape Columbia to the North Pole (April 1909).
Mapped by the German administration.
First to reach the South Pole (14 December 1911) from the Bay of Whales via the Axel Heiberg Glacier, revealing the Queen Maud Mountains.
Penetrated deepest into the Weddell Sea, discovering the Luitpold Coast and the Filchner Ice Shelf, then drifted north in the pack.
Australasian Antarctic Expedition charted the coast from Commonwealth Bay to Queen Mary Land and set up a station on Macquarie Island.
Reached the South Pole on 17 January 1912 via the Beardmore Glacier, 33 days after Amundsen; all five died on the return.

journeys.n: Douglas Mawson; Belgrave Ninnis; Xavier Mertz
journeys.sum: Sledged east across the Mertz and Ninnis glaciers into George V Land; Mawson alone survived the return.
Danish expedition crossed the Greenland ice sheet at its widest, from Dronning Louise Land to the Upernavik district, with glaciological measurements.

journeys.sp: Brazil / American Museum of Natural History
journeys.sum: First descent of the River of Doubt (Rio Roosevelt), a 1,000 km tributary of the Madeira.
Icebreakers Taymyr and Vaygach discovered Severnaya Zemlya (1913) and made the first east to west transit of the Northeast Passage (1914 to 1915).
Endurance was beset and crushed in the Weddell Sea; the crew drifted on the ice to Elephant Island and Shackleton sailed the James Caird to South Georgia.
The telegraph commission of Candido Rondon mapped the interior of Mato Grosso and Goias, 1907 to 1915.
Maud expedition along the Northeast Passage, wintering off Cape Chelyuskin and Ayon Island, with oceanographic work on the Siberian shelf.

journeys.n: Charles Howard-Bury, George Mallory, Guy Bullock, Oliver Wheeler
journeys.sum: First reconnaissance of Everest from Tibet, mapping its northern approaches and finding the route to the North Col.
Dog-sledge journey from Hudson Bay to Nome, recording Inuit communities across Arctic North America.
First motor crossing of the Sahara, by Citroën half-tracks from Touggourt to Timbuktu.
Egyptian diplomat who rediscovered the lost oases of Arkenu and Uweinat on a camel journey from Sollum to Darfur.

journeys.n: Georges-Marie Haardt and Louis Audouin-Dubreuil (Croisière noire)
journeys.sum: Citroën half-track expedition from Colomb-Béchar across the Sahara and the Congo basin to Lake Victoria, filmed and widely publicised.
Up the Rio Negro, Rio Branco and Uraricoera toward the Parima, using the first aircraft and shortwave radio in Amazon exploration.
journeys.g: Pilot Walter Hinton and photographer Albert Stevens flew survey flights from Boa Vista.

journeys.sum: Explored the Tsangpo Gorges round Namcha Barwa, closing most of the gap in the Brahmaputra's course.
Final expedition from Cuiaba into the upper Xingu in search of 'Z'; the party vanished.

journeys.n: Roald Amundsen; Lincoln Ellsworth; Umberto Nobile
journeys.sum: Airship Norge flew from Spitsbergen over the North Pole to Alaska, showing no land in that sector of the central Arctic.
Claimed flight from Spitsbergen to the North Pole and back in May 1926.
First flight over the South Pole (28 to 29 November 1929) from Little America, with aerial survey of the Queen Maud Mountains.
Mapped the valley of the Assassins' castle of Alamut and travelled in Luristan (The Valleys of the Assassins).
First recorded crossing of the Rub' al Khali, from Salalah to Doha.
journeys.g: Guided by Shaikh Salih bin Kalut and Rashidi and Murra Bedouin.

journeys.sum: Sledge surveys from Domashny Island mapped Severnaya Zemlya and showed it was an archipelago.
German Greenland Expedition set up the inland station Eismitte; Wegener died on the return in November 1930.

journeys.n: László Almásy (with Robert Clayton East Clayton, Patrick Clayton, H. W. G. J. Penderel)
journeys.sum: Car and aircraft search for Zerzura that mapped the Gilf Kebir's wadis and in 1933 found the rock paintings of Wadi Sura (Cave of Swimmers).
Model T Ford expedition through the Gilf Kebir, Uweinat, Sarra, Tekro and Erdi, mapping the eastern Sahara by car.
Crossed the Empty Quarter from Hofuf via Jabrin and Shanna westwards to Sulaiyil, finding the Wabar craters on the way.

journeys.n: Mick Leahy; Dan Leahy; Jim Taylor
journeys.sp: Australia (Territory of New Guinea; gold prospecting)
journeys.sum: Following reconnaissance flights, walked into the densely populated Wahgi Valley and Mount Hagen area of the New Guinea Highlands.
British Graham Land Expedition surveyed the west coast of Graham Land and found George VI Sound, showing Graham Land to be a peninsula.
First trans-Antarctic flight, from Dundee Island across the unknown interior of West Antarctica to near Little America.
Travelled inland from Mukalla up the Wadi Do'an to Shibam, Seiyun and Tarim in the Hadhramaut (The Southern Gates of Arabia).

journeys.n: Richard H. Cruzen; Richard E. Byrd
journeys.sum: Large US Navy operation whose aircraft flew to the Pole from Little America and photographed the Marie Byrd Land and Ellsworth Land coasts.
First crossing of the eastern Rub' al Khali from Mughshin to the Liwa oasis, returning through Oman.

journeys.n: David Bunger; Western Group, Operation Highjump
journeys.sum: Western Group seaplanes photographed the East Antarctic coast, including the ice-free Bunger Hills.
Second crossing of the Empty Quarter, from the Hadhramaut to Sulaiyil and on across the sands to Abu Dhabi.
Aerial photography and mapping of the Canadian north in the 1940s and 1950s.
Topographic maps of all of Alaska from aerial photography, completed in the 1950s.
First overland crossing of Antarctica by tractor, from Shackleton Base on the Weddell Sea via the South Pole to Scott Base.
New Zealand support party laid depots up the Skelton Glacier and drove modified farm tractors to the South Pole.

moments.x: Austronesian voyagers move south into the Philippines: the start of the greatest seafaring expansion before 1500.
The starting point for Europe: the Mycenaean and Minoan seas, known from pottery, palaces and Egyptian and Hittite records.
Herodotus reports Phoenicians sent by Pharaoh Necho sailing round Africa. Nobody followed, and the knowledge was lost.
Pytheas sails to Britain and the northern ocean; Alexander's army and Nearchus's fleet carry Greek eyes to the Indus.
The Han envoy reaches Ferghana and Bactria and brings back the first Chinese account of Central Asia.
Ptolemy's Geography sums up what Rome knew, from Ireland to the edge of China.
Norse sailors reach North America. The sagas kept the memory, but Europe's maps lost it.
Polynesian voyagers settle New Zealand, the last large land on Earth to be settled.
Thirty years of travel from Tangier to China, the widest account of the medieval Islamic world.
The Ming treasure fleets sail to India, Arabia and East Africa, then stop.
Dias rounds the southern tip of Africa; ten years later da Gama reaches India with a Gujarati pilot.
Columbus crosses the Atlantic; Europe's map of the sea starts to grow faster than its map of the land.
Magellan's fleet crosses the Pacific, the largest single blank on the map.
Cook's three voyages chart New Zealand, eastern Australia and the high southern ocean, with Tupaia as navigator on the first.
Lewis and Clark cross to the Pacific, with Sacagawea and Shoshone and Nez Perce guides.
The decades of fastest growth: Livingstone, Stanley, Barth and many others cross the African interior.
Amundsen and Scott reach the South Pole; flights soon cross the Arctic and Antarctica.
Where the map stops. Every dark cell was known to the people who lived there.

places: San Ramón de la Nueva Orán
